You'll continuously improve the launch playbook and incorporate state-specific regulatory and market considerations into acquisition strategy. 🔎 SEO Strategy You'll own SEO strategy and keyword priorities for the pages that actually drive enrollment. You'll guide technical SEO recommendations across program and state pages, including schema, metadata, heading structure, internal linking, URL structure, and on-page conventions. You'll also help shape page templates and layouts so our programs can be found—not just by Google, but by the increasingly important world of AI-powered search. 🧪 Website Conversion & CRO You'll own conversion strategy for our highest-impact program pages. You'll analyze funnels, run A/B tests, experiment with landing pages, and partner with the team to ship experiences that turn more visitors into applicants. 💌 Lifecycle & Email You'll own lifecycle marketing across nurture, re-engagement, TOFU, MOFU, and referral journeys. You'll build segmented, automated experiences that help move families from first interaction to enrollment—and turn happy families into advocates. 🗣️ Word of Mouth & Referral Some of our strongest growth comes from families telling other families. Co-ops, Facebook groups, neighbors, the mom at the park. It's one of our most important channels, and we don't want it to be an accident. You'll own making it deliberate: building referral mechanics into lifecycle flows, working alongside our ambassador program. It already works. Your job is to make it compound. 💰 Paid Acquisition & Agency Management You'll manage our paid media agency, establish growth targets, review performance, and push for better results. You'll continuously test creative, audiences, and channels to increase awareness, qualified applications, and enrollment while improving efficiency. 📊 Analytics & Reporting You'll own state-level pipeline reporting and turn data into decisions. You'll track traffic, conversion by page and source, lead-to-enrollment rates, paid performance, word-of-mouth, referrals, and other acquisition sources. In other words: You won't just report what happened. You'll tell us what we should do about it. How We'll Know You're Winning You'll help us: Grow awareness and reach in target markets Generate more qualified applications Successfully launch new states Improve website and funnel conversion Increase lead-to-enrollment conversion Improve marketing efficiency as markets mature Build repeatable systems that make every launch better than the last Who Are You? You're someone who: Has 5+ years of B2C/DTC growth or performance marketing experience acquiring consumers at scale (with B2C experience within the last 5 years) Has managed multiple markets, regions, or campaigns simultaneously Knows paid search and paid social and has a track record of generating qualified leads Has managed agencies or external partners against performance goals Understands SEO strategy and technical SEO fundamentals Has hands-on CRO, A/B testing, and landing-page experience Has built lifecycle and email programs using marketing automation tools Loves analytics and knows how to turn numbers into action Has Webflow experience (strongly preferred) Is ridiculously organized—you set dates, own deadlines, and actually hit them Can juggle multiple channels, campaigns, and launches without losing your mind Is comfortable working independently and figuring things out This Role Will Make You Very Happy If... You are a builder. You don't want to spend your day managing someone else's strategy. You want to build the landing page. Launch the campaign. Write the brief. Pull the data. Spot the problem. Run the test. Fix the funnel. And see what happens. You like having an opinion—and you're perfectly comfortable changing it when the data proves you wrong. You care deeply about helping families access better educational options. You like moving fast without sacrificing quality. And the idea of owning growth across an expanding portfolio of states sounds less like "a lot of work" and more like: "Where do I sign?" Our Culture: High Standards. Low Ego. Culture at OpenEd is intentional. It's defined by what we promote—and what we tolerate. Our latest eNPS of 77 places OpenEd in the top 0.1% of technology companies. We don't put values on a wall and forget about them. We actually use them. Customer First Be obsessed with creating value for learners and families. Hard Choices, Easy Life Address difficult things directly, quickly, and transparently. I Did > We Should Ideas are great. Execution is better. Learn Out Loud Share what you're learning. Give feedback. Leave your ego at the door. Prioritize Ruthlessly Do a few important things exceptionally well. Fast AND World Class Move quickly. Don't lower the bar. Strong Opinions, Weakly Held Make the case. Listen. Change your mind when the evidence says you should. Make Others Famous Make the people around you better—and make sure they get the credit. The Team & Your Autonomy: You'll join a team of five. That's it. Five people covering growth, content, paid, lifecycle, referral, and the ambassador program across a 13-state footprint. A lean, mean marketing machine. Which means two things. First, you'll have real ownership from day one. There's no layer between you and the work. Second, you'll never be doing it alone. This is a team that genuinely collaborates. We share what's working, steal each other's good ideas, and make each other better. (See: Make Others Famous. ) You'll work closely with the Director, Growth Marketing on strategy and priorities, but this is not a "wait for permission" kind of role. You'll have significant day-to-day autonomy to experiment, iterate, and ship based on data. You'll personally stand up pages, campaigns, lifecycle flows, and launch programs while managing external agencies where they can extend your reach. You own execution across a growing portfolio of states. Translation: If you see something that needs to happen, we're looking for someone who makes it happen. What We Offer: Competitive salary 401(k) with company matching opportunities Comprehensive medical, dental, vision, life, critical illness, accident, STD/LTD, HSA, and FSA benefits Fully remote work environment Flexible working hours with an emphasis on healthy work-life balance Generous PTO A collaborative, supportive team where your work actually matters Ready to Open More Doors? If you're a hands-on growth marketer who loves data, moves quickly, builds things, asks "why?", and gets a little too excited about improving conversion rates... We should talk. There are a lot more families out there looking for a better way to educate their children. Let's help them find it. EEO Statement OpenEd is an equal opportunity employer. - Drive GTM campaigns and product launches, coordinating across product, design, growth, and sales to drive awareness and self-service adoption.

- Craft messaging and positioning for Reducto products that resonates with both technical personas (AI/ML engineers, software developers, data engineers, etc.) and enterprise buyer personas (executive buyers, product managers, line of business owners, etc.).

- Develop ICP and persona intelligence, mapping buyer journeys for both self-service users and enterprise customers.

- Work closely with GTM ops team to measure our impact to the sales & marketing funnel (web traffic, leads, sales opportunities, etc.) and implement improvements to accelerate conversion rates at each stage of the funnel.

- Support sales enablement initiative that equip our teams to win: pitch decks, customer stories, competitive intelligence, and objection handling.

You’ll Thrive Here If You:

- Hold yourself to a high bar for quality and precision.

- Enjoy solving complex problems and building from first principles.

- Have 5+ years of experience in product marketing.

- Use AI thoughtfully in your own workflows to amplify your output and the quality of your programs.

- Operate well in fast-changing, high-growth environments.

- Collaborate effectively across technical and non-technical teams.

- Take full ownership from strategy through execution.

Bonus points if you:

- Have built product marketing function from scratch at an early-stage startup.

- Have experience marketing AI/ML, infrastructure, or document processing products

- Are fluent with marketing tooling - CRM platforms (eg Salesforce, Attio), interactive demos (eg Arcade, Storylane), web analytics (eg Google Analytics, PostHog), lead enrichment (eg Clay, Default), and data analysis & reporting (eg Hex).

- Care deeply about combining technical excellence with business impact.

Why Reducto

- Impact: Your work directly shapes how the world’s best AI companies access and use enterprise data.

- Speed: We move fast, ship often, and iterate in days, not months.

- Learning: Work alongside world-class engineers, operators, and founders who care deeply about product, precision, and velocity.

- Daily Lunch, enjoy free lunch with teammates in the office.

- Commuter Reimbursement, we’ll cover your transportation costs.

- Comprehensive Insurance, medical, dental, and vision.

- Health and Wellness Budget, up to $150 per month for wellness spending such as gym memberships or fitness classes.

- Parental Leave, flexible scheduling that works for you and your family.

This is an in-person role based in our San Francisco office. We’re an early-stage company, we move fast and work hard. Please apply only if that excites you.

You will take ownership of that relationship — directing, elevating, and when needed, challenging the agency's output — while also building Range's internal creative capability. You will be the internal authority on what great advertising looks and sounds like for Range: what angle to take, what visual language resonates, what copy earns a click, and how the story holds together from the first impression all the way through the homepage, landing page, and member registration.

You will concept campaigns, write or direct copy, set the visual direction, and ensure our brand promise is consistent and compelling across every paid touchpoint. You will partner closely with our performance marketing team, who will handle media buying and channel execution — your job is to make sure the creative they're running is exceptional.

Provide strategic direction for copywriting and content marketing — ensuring our messaging speaks directly to high-income earners, tech professionals, and executives in a way that feels modern, credible, and trustworthy.

You will work closely with product and growth teams to close any gaps in that narrative and reduce no-show rates.

Stay Culturally Sharp. Stay ahead of advertising trends, platform creative formats, and cultural moments. You know what's resonating on Meta, YouTube, and LinkedIn right now — and you know how to apply those instincts to a premium brand without losing credibility or trust.

Generate a Continuous Stream of Fresh Creative. Range needs a steady pipeline of new ad concepts in market at all times. You will build a system for generating, testing, and refreshing creative — partnering with performance marketing to understand what's working and using those insights to sharpen future concepts.

You can write a compelling headline, a clear value proposition, and a landing page that converts — and you know when the agency's draft isn't good enough. You understand how to balance brand storytelling with direct response principles.

- Cultural Awareness. You know what's trending, what's resonating, and what feels dated. You bring a fresh, modern sensibility to everything you touch, and you're not afraid to push Range's creative in a bolder direction.

- Full-Funnel Thinking. You understand how advertising connects to the broader member journey. You think about the ad-to-landing-page-to-registration flow as a single creative system, not a series of disconnected assets.

- Collaborative by Nature. You work well with performance marketing, product, and leadership teams. You can translate data and business goals into creative direction, and you can translate creative decisions into language that resonates with non-creative stakeholders.

- Startup Adaptability. You thrive in a fast-moving environment where you own your domain, make decisions with incomplete information, and ship work quickly. You've operated in a growth-stage company or built an in-house creative capability from scratch.

Location

McLean, VA

Employment Type

Full time

Department

Design

At Range, we’re building towards a world where anyone can live the financial life they imagine for themselves. If that sounds like a mission you want to be a part of, let’s create it together.

We’re building AI-powered wealth management. Investments, taxes, retirement, estate planning, all in one platform instead of scattered across different advisors and apps. We're backed by Google's Gradient Ventures, Cathay Innovation, Scale Venture Partners, and more. We’re growing fast while still small enough that everyone's work is visible and impactful.

About the Role

We are looking for a senior, strategic Creative Director to own the creative vision for how Range shows up in the world. This is a rare opportunity to build an in-house advertising function from the ground up at a well-funded, hyper-growth fintech company.

Today, our ad creative is managed by an external agency. You will take ownership of that relationship — directing, elevating, and when needed, challenging the agency's output — while also building Range's internal creative capability. You will be the internal authority on what great advertising looks and sounds like for Range: what angle to take, what visual language resonates, what copy earns a click, and how the story holds together from the first impression all the way through the homepage, landing page, and member registration.

This is not a production role. You are a creative director and strategic thinker first. You will concept campaigns, write or direct copy, set the visual direction, and ensure our brand promise is consistent and compelling across every paid touchpoint. You will partner closely with our performance marketing team, who will handle media buying and channel execution — your job is to make sure the creative they're running is exceptional.

You know what's cool. You understand trends. You have strong instincts about what earns attention and what earns trust, and you know how to apply both to a premium financial brand.

What You'll Do

Own Range's Marketing Creative. Take full ownership of the creative strategy and output for Range's performance ads — from paid social and video to landing pages and registration flows. You are the internal creative lead, and everything that runs in the market reflects your direction and standards.

Direct Agency Partners. Manage our relationship with external creative agencies, providing clear, confident briefs and elevating their output to meet Range's bar. You know how to get the best work out of agency partners and when to push back.

Set the Creative and Copy Direction. Develop and maintain a clear, compelling point of view on Range's advertising voice and visual language. Provide strategic direction for copywriting and content marketing — ensuring our messaging speaks directly to high-income earners, tech professionals, and executives in a way that feels modern, credible, and trustworthy.

Ensure Full-Funnel Creative Cohesion. Oversee the creative journey from ad to homepage to registration. The promise we make in an ad must be the experience a prospective member has when they arrive. You will work closely with product and growth teams to close any gaps in that narrative and reduce no-show rates.

Stay Culturally Sharp. Stay ahead of advertising trends, platform creative formats, and cultural moments. You know what's resonating on Meta, YouTube, and LinkedIn right now — and you know how to apply those instincts to a premium brand without losing credibility or trust.

Generate a Continuous Stream of Fresh Creative. Range needs a steady pipeline of new ad concepts in market at all times. You will build a system for generating, testing, and refreshing creative — partnering with performance marketing to understand what's working and using those insights to sharpen future concepts.

Collaborate Cross-Functionally. Partner with performance marketing, product, and content teams to ensure creative strategy and business strategy are aligned. You may embed with product pods and will be a key voice in shaping how Range communicates its value to prospective members.

What Will Set You Apart

- Advertising Creative Leadership. You have a track record of concepting and directing advertising campaigns — not just executing them. You've led agencies or in-house creative teams and know how to set a standard and hold people to it.

- Brand and Copy Instincts. You have strong, confident opinions about messaging. You can write a compelling headline, a clear value proposition, and a landing page that converts — and you know when the agency's draft isn't good enough. You understand how to balance brand storytelling with direct response principles.

- Cultural Awareness. You know what's trending, what's resonating, and what feels dated. You bring a fresh, modern sensibility to everything you touch, and you're not afraid to push Range's creative in a bolder direction.

- Full-Funnel Thinking. You understand how advertising connects to the broader member journey. You think about the ad-to-landing-page-to-registration flow as a single creative system, not a series of disconnected assets.

- Collaborative by Nature. You work well with performance marketing, product, and leadership teams. You can translate data and business goals into creative direction, and you can translate creative decisions into language that resonates with non-creative stakeholders.

- Startup Adaptability. You thrive in a fast-moving environment where you own your domain, make decisions with incomplete information, and ship work quickly. You've operated in a growth-stage company or built an in-house creative capability from scratch.

- Experience: 7+ years in creative direction, art direction, or advertising — ideally with experience at a consumer brand, premium fintech, or growth-stage startup. Agency background with in-house ambitions, or in-house experience with agency fluency, both welcome.

Compensation

Base salary range: $170,000 – $270,000

This is the base salary range we expect in good faith to pay for this role at the time of posting. Where an offer lands within the range depends on the scope and complexity of work the candidate can own independently and demonstrated depth at this level.

Other compensation and benefits

The range above reflects base salary only. Our offer packages also include equity in the form of stock options, so total compensation for this role will exceed the base salary range.

We do not ask for or consider salary history. You are welcome to ask questions about compensation at any point in the process.

Benefits

- Comprehensive health coverage: Medical, dental and vision

- 401k plan

- Technology allowance

- PTO

- Top of Market Pay

- Paid parental leave

- In-person team & company events

The Marketing Analytics role will play a pivotal role in driving growth strategy. Responsible for supporting marketing strategies and execution across paid and organic channels, while owning the data infrastructure, reporting, and analytics that inform and optimize efforts.

  - Experience with SQL and Python to build data pipelines, extract and clean raw marketing data, and conduct advanced quantitative analysis

  - Experience with managing and analyzing intricate datasets

  - Experience with paid acquisition channels, including campaign setup, optimization, and measurement

  - Experience with HTML

  - Experience with Metabase, Looker, or similar BI platforms

  - Experience with performing analytics for both large companies as well as high-growth startups.

Other compensation and benefits

About Solink

At Solink, our mission is to safeguard what matters most. We provide businesses with the tools to know sooner and act faster by transforming video security into real-time operational insights.

Our cloud-based platform integrates seamlessly with your existing cameras and systems, turning them into intelligent sensors that detect and interpret key moments. This empowers teams to make data-driven decisions, enhance security, and improve operational efficiency.

Trusted by over 35,000 locations across 60+ countries - including brands like McDonald’s and JYSK - Solink delivers clarity when it counts. Our solutions help businesses reduce shrink, optimize performance, and respond proactively to potential threats.

We're growing rapidly, earning industry recognition, and scaling with purpose. We’ve been recognized by Deloitte’s Fast 50™ and Fast 500™, Business Intelligence Group, and as one of Ottawa’s Best Places to Work. And we’re just getting started!

About The Role

Solink is looking for a (head of) Senior Director, Product Marketing and Customer Marketing to create category leadership and sharpen our positioning - accelerating adoption, differentiation, and revenue across our key products. This is a newly unified leadership role, bringing Product Marketing and Customer Marketing together so the story we tell to prospects and the story we tell to existing customers reinforce each other.

You'll own positioning and messaging, lead go-to-market strategy for major launches, run competitive intelligence and win/loss, scale sales enablement, and stand up an Analyst Relations (AR) program - while also owning how we market to and grow our existing customer base through advocacy, references, and expansion programs.

This is a senior, executive-facing role for someone who can define a category, arm a sales team to win, and build a team and function from a strong existing base of product marketers.

What You’ll Be Doing

Positioning & Messaging

- Own product positioning, messaging, and narrative across Solink’s platform and key products and industries we serve.

- Develop and defend a category point of view that differentiates Solink from adjacent and competing solutions.

- Test and refine messaging with customers, prospects, and sales to ensure it resonates and converts.

GTM Strategy

- Lead go-to-market strategy and execution for major feature and product launches, partnering with Product, Demand Gen, Sales, and Customer Success.

- Build launch playbooks and processes that scale across a growing product portfolio.

- Identify opportunities to grow adoption and ARPU through positioning, packaging, and GTM for new features and add-ons.

Competitive Intelligence

- Own Solink’s competitive intelligence program, keeping a current, accurate view of the competitive landscape.

- Run a win/loss program that turns deal outcomes into sharper positioning and enablement.

- Educate internal teams - Sales, Marketing, Product - on competitive threats and how to respond to them.

Sales Enablement

Success in this role requires strong commercial acumen, deep collaboration with Sales, and a performance-driven mindset grounded in measurable pipeline and revenue impact.

- Own the execution for Superhuman Mail, aligning with GTM goals and revenue targets.

- Collaborate with cross-functional partners to build and run full-funnel marketing campaigns across paid, earned, and owned channels, driving shared ownership of inbound and outbound pipeline for net-new acquisition and account expansion.

- Partner closely with Sales and RevOps to align campaign strategy with pipeline goals and account priorities.

- Build and optimize nurture programs that accelerate leads through the funnel and drive customer expansion.

- Measure and report on campaign performance, pipeline impact, and ROI—turning insights into action.

- Collaborate cross-functionally with Sales, Customer Success, Product, Product Marketing, Content, Brand, Growth, and other teams to deliver a cohesive buyer experience.

- Translate product strategy and roadmap into revenue-generating demand programs

- Partner closely with Sales leadership to design high-impact Sales Plays

- Launch rapid, test-and-learn campaigns tied to product launches, feature releases, and market opportunities

- Run performance-oriented programs that can scale into integrated campaigns and buyer journeys

- Continuously optimize messaging, segmentation, and channel mix based on performance data

3. Competitive & Market Plays

- Develop competitive displacement programs

- Enable Sales with targeted plays, messaging, and field-ready assets

- Partner with Product Marketing on positioning and differentiation

- Design expansion and cross-sell programs across the installed base

- Partner with Customer Success and Sales to drive product adoption and revenue growth

- Build targeted segmentation strategies based on product usage and account signals

- Marketing-sourced product pipeline (and revenue)

- Marketing-influenced product pipeline (and revenue)

- Product campaign performance and ROI

- Conversion rates across key funnel stages

Qualifications

- Deep expertise in product demand—tailoring messaging and programs to different personas, segments, and stages of the funnel. Skilled at turning product strategy into compelling demand programs.

- Experience partnering deeply with Sales in a sales-led GTM motion.

- Strong analytical orientation with experience using data to drive decisions and optimize campaigns. Proven experience owning performance metrics.

- Experience running agile campaign frameworks and rapid experimentation

- Strong partnership skills—comfortable aligning closely with Sales, RevOps, Product Marketing, Product, Customer Success, Lifecycle, Content, Brand, Creative, Growth, and Channel Partner teams; proven ability in cross-functional leadership and orchestration to keep stakeholders aligned.

- Executive presence and ability to influence cross-functional stakeholders

- Customer-obsessed with a deep commitment to understanding user pain points and delivering value at every touchpoint.

- Comfortable with ambiguity, adaptable, and proactive in creating clarity amid change.

- Demonstrated ability to balance vision with execution, delivering results while holding themselves and teams accountable; skilled at prioritizing effectively under constraints.

- Familiarity with tools like Pardot, Salesforce, 6sense, and other platforms.

- Proven track record of influencing pipeline and revenue through ABX programs — you can point to specific accounts won or accelerated as a result of your programs

- Experience working closely with enterprise sales teams; you are fluent in sales language and understand how deals move

- Familiarity with the ABM tech stack: tools such as 6sense, Demandbase, Terminus, Salesforce, HubSpot or Marketo, Outreach or Salesloft, and intent data platforms.

- Project management fluency — you can run multiple concurrent programs across different account tiers without dropping the ball

- Experience partnering cross-functionally with peer teams like Customer Advocacy and Customer Education, plus Product, Data, Sales, and Customer Success, to ship aligned customer communications.

About Titan Banking AI

The financial system is the backbone of America’s economy, yet today’s AI is ungoverned, unaccountable, and unfit for banking and financial services.

Titan was founded to change that.

We are doing this by offering a purpose-built, bank-native AI Platform as a Service that enables financial institutions and fintechs to innovate safely, scale efficiently, and strengthen their role in serving their customers and communities.

We are seeking an events and demand generation senior marketer with banking or financial services experience to build our events program and supporting demand generation activities from the ground up, from national industry conferences to intimate executive gatherings and our first annual client summit.

This is an opportunity to join a team of industry experts providing a best-in-class solution to leading customers and innovators. AI is changing everything and we will help our customers deliver outsized impact and achieve transformative business outcomes.

The Role

- Own the event and field programming end to end. Own planning and activation across national industry conferences, regional field events, technical community builder nights, and Titan’s inaugural client summit.

- Run the demand generation that connects to it. Lead sponsored webinars with banking trade publishers and our LinkedIn paid program against named target accounts.

- Design for a senior audience. Our buyers are bank CEOs, chief risk officers, chief compliance officers, and boards.

- Drive impact. You’ll sit on the growth team and have a direct line of sight into the impact your programs drive.

What You Will Own

- Industry conferences and tradeshows. Across the national fintech, banking association, and regional circuits. You'll select and negotiate sponsorships, run booth and activation logistics, identify speaking opportunities, brief sales on target accounts, and own the follow-up program that turns attendance into pipeline.

- Executive field program. Regional briefings for bank leadership, run as a touring series across 4-6 target markets. You'll partner with sales to identify the markets, select venues, build the guest lists, and design a format worth a bank CEO's afternoon.

- Annual client summit. An invitation-only gathering of senior bankers, Titan’s own thought leadership event and select guest list.

- Technical community series. A recurring evening series in our NYC office for bank engineers and data leaders, followed by an executive dinner. Designed to build a community among our more technical users.

- Sponsored webinars. Co-branded sessions with banking trade publishers. You'll own topic selection, speaker recruitment, promotion, and the gated asset that follows.

- LinkedIn paid. Always-on and account-based campaigns against our target institution list, coordinated with the event calendar.

- Budget and vendor management. Negotiate sponsorship contracts, publisher agreements, and venues.

What We Are Looking For

Required

- Seven or more years in B2B marketing with a majority in events, including owning a program end to end.

- Experience marketing to financial institutions, or to a regulated enterprise buyer with a comparable sales cycle.

- A track record with C-level audiences: you've curated and produced executive-format, high-touch events.

- Budget ownership at six or seven figures, including sponsorship negotiations.

- Comfort with a growth team as your closest partner, and with being goaled on pipeline impact.

- Willingness to roll up your sleeves, manage programs end-to-end, collaborate with a cross-functional team to accomplish a goal.

Strongly Preferred

1. Familiarity with the banking conference circuit, particularly the ABA and Bank Director ecosystems.

2. Experience running technical or developer community programming.

3. Hands-on experience with LinkedIn Campaign Manager.

4. Proven success managing and scaling an events program.

What Success Looks Like

You'll build and scale Titan's events program from the ground up, partnering closely with the CMO to fine-tune and execute the 2027 plan.

Your first year is heavy and hands-on, fully owning industry events, roadshows, webinars, and LinkedIn. As the program scales, so will this role and the supporting marketing team.

Why Titan

- Seed-stage ownership: you will build the marketing function, not inherit it.

- Direct access to leadership: you will work closely with the CGO, CMO, and sales team, not through layers of management.

- A category worth owning: banking AI is one of the most consequential verticals in enterprise software, and Titan is defining how it should be done.

Compensation Range: $140K - $160K

1906.FireCrawl Job Description: About Tin Can Tin Can is building a safer, simpler way for kids to connect — without smartphones. We’re creating screen-free, delightful devices and services that let families call the people who matter most, free from the noise of today’s digital world. We’re building a bold, authentic, nostalgic, and kinda quirky brand that resonates with folks who want something simpler & better for their kids than the tech-infused lives we’re currently living (and who have a sense of humor about it). As we gear up to scale to thousands of families, we’re ready to bring on a Brand Marketing Manager to help make it happen. The Role We're looking for a Brand Marketing Manager who's just as happy staring at a blank whiteboard dreaming up something delightful as they are staring at a Gantt chart making sure that idea actually happens. You'll report to our Head of Brand Strategy & Communications and work closely and collaboratively with teams across the company. This isn't a "take the brief and go" role. We want someone with real creative judgment, someone who gets Tin Can, relishes the weird and wonderful challenge we're up against, and feels how lucky we are to be handing kids the chance to build real, meaningful connections. You'll help us decide who we team up with, how we bring product moments to life (online and IRL), and how we keep parents and kids engaged in unexpected ways. You're a big thinker and a doer in equal measure. Building the workback plan delights you almost as much as pitching the idea that needed one. You write clearly, you communicate constantly, and you know an idea is only as good as its execution. If you keep a mental file of what iconic, boundary-pushing brands do right, get energy from doing five different things before 11am, don't need hand-holding, and take real pride in the follow-through — we should definitely get on the phone. What You'll Do Partnerships & collaborations. Bring us the unexpected, brand-true partnership ideas we haven't thought of yet, and go build relationships with the people and companies who share our values. You know what's right for Tin Can on instinct, and you move on it. Project management & campaign coordination. Keep every brand initiative on track across a dozen moving pieces — timelines, stakeholders, the works — so things get from brief to launch without a single dropped ball. You're the glue between creative and strategy, and you help us hit aggressive deadlines with gusto! Campaign briefs. Turn our best ideas into briefs that lay out the why, how, and what clearly enough that creative work has a strategic foundation before it ever hits production. Brand influencers. Manage our top-tier celebrity and influencer relationships and turn our most high-profile customers into our loudest advocates. Find new, authentic ways to pull them into our world. Brand stewardship. You are the Tin Can brand out in the world — newsletter, partner decks, campaign assets, all of it — making sure the experience feels like us whether it's someone's first touchpoint or their one-hundred-and-sixty-seventh. Reporting & tracking. Own the post-campaign wrap-up across your world; what worked, what didn't, and why, so we're always getting sharper. What We're Looking For 4–6 years of marketing experience, ideally at a consumer brand, DTC startup, or agency with consumer clients. You've had your hands in enough of the marketing mix to know what good looks like, and you're always thinking up new ways to do it well. Strong writing and verbal skills. Everything from a cold outreach email to a campaign brief sounds like it came from the same brand. You’re not necessarily a copywriter but you’re not not good at copywriting. A creative point of view. You get us, and you have real opinions on how we show up in the world. You know what's cool, and you never forget we're talking to two audiences at once: parents and kids. Brand, brand, brand. You get why it matters more than almost anything else here, and you take real ownership over how we evolve and grow it. Comfort with celebrity and partnership work. You've navigated brand-partner relationships before and know how to keep a conversation moving. Even better: you already have a running list of ideas for our growing roster of famous Tin Can households. Serious project management instincts. You build the tracker, set the deadline, and chase people down without being asked twice. A collaborative, low-ego approach. You'll be in and out of every function constantly — trust is as much a part of the job as taste is. An ownership mindset. Helping build Tin Can's brand marketing function from here is genuinely exciting to you. Comfort with ambiguity and a bias toward action. The playbook's still being written. We need someone who sees that as the fun part. If the idea of shaping the Tin Can brand at a genuinely pivotal moment gives you butterflies, we want to hear from you!

- Build, maintain, and optimize lifecycle automations including welcome series, abandoned cart, post-purchase, post-activation, loyalty and repeat purchase, referral, and other customer journey programs

- Create and refine customer segmentation strategies to deliver personalized communications that improve engagement, retention, and customer lifetime value

Performance Marketing Manager

Seattle

Compensation

About Tin Can

Here at Tin Can, we're working to give kids the social independence we had growing up—without smartphones. We've built a remix of the classic home phone we had when we were young, but on a totally private network and with a bunch of added safety functionality (plus some fun surprise features in the pipeline).

We're building a bold, authentic, nostalgic, and kinda quirky brand that resonates with folks who want something simpler & better for their kids than the tech-infused lives we're currently living (and who have a sense of humor about it). As we gear up to reach more families at home and abroad, we're ready to bring on someone to take our paid acquisition program from "working" to "unmistakably a machine."

The Role

We're looking for a Performance Marketing Manager to turn our paid acquisition program into a reliable, scaled growth engine. Paid is already one of our fastest-growing ways of reaching new families, and it's set for serious growth starting this Q4 and carrying into 2027 and beyond. The machine is built and it has real momentum—your job is to take what's working and make it a whole lot bigger.

This is a hands-on seat. You'll be in the accounts, in the data, and in the creative reviews—not steering from a dashboard three layers up.

Key Responsibilities

- Own paid social on Meta. Optimize it continuously, using performance data to guide targeting, budget, and creative decisions—and stay ahead of whatever the platform changes next.

- Keep the creative pipeline full. Partner with our in-house influencer team and external partners so there's always a steady stream of ads flowing through the account that perform _and_ look like us.

- Push beyond Meta. Test new platforms, scale the ones that earn their place, and build a diversified engine that doesn't wobble when one channel does.

- Build the dashboards you need (if they don’t already exist, which they probably do) to catch what's working, and what isn't, in near real time with the support of an analytics team and tooling that make this genuinely painless.

- Own budget planning and pacing across channels, allocating spend against performance and growth targets.

- Partner with Brand to amplify bigger campaigns and moments through paid, in lockstep with organic, influencer, lifecycle, and PR.

What We're Looking For

- 4–6+ years in performance marketing, with deep hands-on fluency in paid social as your primary domain—and a reaction to new channels that's closer to "ooh" than "ugh."

- End-to-end ownership. You've run a paid acquisition program yourself, strategy through execution.

- Data and creative, both. You back every decision with the numbers, and you just know a good ad when you see one.

- An eye for brand. This is a performance role first, but you're also protecting our tone and look as things move fast—catching what's off-brand before it goes live.

- Low-ego and collaborative. This seat is highly cross-functional. You push for what you need while being respectful of everyone else's time and priorities.

What You'll Have to Work With

- Budget: The budget limit does not exist. If the CAC math works, we'll keep pouring fuel on the fire.

- Data & Analytics: You won't have to fight for data. Between Hex and our existing dashboards, there's no ask too small and no chart too complicated to stand up—fast.

- Creative: If the current pipeline can't keep pace with what paid needs, you have the standing to ask for more—and get it.

- Growth: Grow the paid engine and the next step is building and leading a team of your own. This starts as a seat where you're doing the work yourself, with real room to grow beyond it.

Why Join Tin Can?

- We're building tech that protects childhood. We're on a quest to give kids a more analog childhood—one with real conversations, real connection, and way less screen time. This is a rare chance to build something that truly matters.

- A seat with real reach. Paid is how most families meet us for the first time. You own that first impression and the growth that follows—not one narrow slice of it.

- Small, high-trust team. Every company says "team," but at Tin Can it means something different. We're a small, mission-driven group that genuinely has each other's backs—professionally and personally. Your ideas and instincts matter from day one.

If you're ready to build the engine that introduces Tin Can to the next hundred thousand families, we'd love to hear from you. Reach out with your resume and a short note on the paid program you're proudest of—what you inherited, what you changed, and what it looks like now.

Compensation Range: $113K - $142K

X-LAB is the new inflection point for the category.

See an insider’s look of our factory: Youtube Video

_

XDS is seeking a Product Marketing Manager to own how our products are positioned, launched, and brought to life across the U.S. market and beyond. In this highly cross-functional role, you will sit at the intersection of product, marketing, sales, creative, and our dealer network, translating world-class engineering and technology into compelling stories that riders and retailers can understand and get excited about.

We are looking for a product-first marketer who understands cycling, knows what makes a great bike compelling beyond a spec sheet, and can turn technical differentiation into clear consumer value. You will help shape X-LAB’s product narrative, manage go-to-market execution across our growing portfolio, and build the systems that ensure every launch is coordinated across our global organization.

This role reports to the Global Head of Marketing, and is based onsite in Los Angeles 5 days a week.

What You’ll Do

- Own product positioning, messaging, and go-to-market strategy across X-LAB’s road, gravel, electric, city, and emerging product categories.

- Translate technical specifications, engineering innovations, materials, and manufacturing advantages into compelling rider-facing and dealer-facing product stories.

- Lead cross-functional product launches from initial planning through market introduction, coordinating Product, Marketing, Design, Ecommerce, PR, Sales, Operations, and Customer Service.

- Develop product marketing assets including product briefs, launch materials, sales tools, dealer education, FAQs, comparison guides, catalogs, and website/PDP content.

- Partner closely with the China product and engineering teams to understand the product roadmap, identify key differentiators, and ensure U.S. market needs and feedback inform future development.

- Maintain a deep understanding of the competitive landscape, including product specifications, pricing, positioning, technology, and emerging category trends.

- Work directly with dealers, riders, media, athletes, and internal teams to gather market feedback and translate insights into actionable product recommendations.

- Support media launches, product reviews, demo programs, trade shows, dealer events, and other product-focused activations.

- Establish and maintain the product marketing calendar, launch processes, asset requirements, and cross-functional go/no-go milestones.

- Help define how X-LAB’s broader product portfolio fits together, ensuring each model has a clear role, audience, value proposition, and reason to exist.

You’re a Great Fit With:

- 5+ years of experience in product marketing, product management, or related roles within cycling, sporting goods, outdoor, mobility, or another product-driven industry with heavy consumer touchpoints (MANDATORY).

- Deep knowledge of bicycles and cycling, including major categories, components, specifications, technologies, competitive brands, and rider needs.

- Proven experience bringing physical products to market and coordinating complex cross-functional launches by building and project managing a world-class product launch engine.

- Exceptional ability to translate technical product features into clear, differentiated consumer benefits and compelling storytelling.

- Strong understanding of positioning, pricing, competitive analysis, customer segmentation, and go-to-market strategy.

- Experience developing product marketing materials across ecommerce, retail, sales, PR, and dealer channels.

- Strong project management skills with the ability to manage multiple products, launches, stakeholders, and deadlines simultaneously.

- Experience working directly with product designers, engineers, sales teams, creative teams, retailers, and senior leadership.

You’re a Spectacular Fit With:

- A genuine passion for cycling and the ability to speak credibly with everyone from a first-time rider to a bike shop owner, engineer, journalist, or WorldTour mechanic.

- Experience working with international product development or manufacturing teams, particularly across Asia and North America.

- Fluency in Mandarin or experience collaborating closely with China-based teams.

- An instinct for identifying not only what makes a product better, but why that difference should matter to someone.

Success Metrics

- Establish a repeatable, cross-functional product launch process with clear ownership, timelines, deliverables, and go/no-go milestones within the first 90 days.

- Ensure every X-LAB product has clearly defined positioning, target rider, competitive set, key differentiators, and consumer-facing value proposition.

- Deliver coordinated, on-time product launches across website, media, dealer, sales, creative, and operational channels.

- Build a comprehensive competitive intelligence system covering key products, pricing, specifications, technologies, and market movements.

- Create an effective feedback loop between U.S. dealers and riders and X-LAB’s global product and engineering teams to influence future product development.

- Increase the consistency and effectiveness with which X-LAB translates its manufacturing and engineering advantages into product stories that drive rider demand, dealer confidence, and market differentiation.

_

Our Compensation and Benefits

- Competitive salary

- Demo bike fleet and comprehensive travel allowances

- Generous time off policy

- Comprehensive medical, dental, and vision coverage

- Office space in beautiful Santa Monica, CA

Equal Opportunity

XDS is an equal opportunity employer. We celebrate diversity and are committed to creating an inclusive environment for all team members.

Senior Product Marketing Manager

Location

North America

Employment Type

Full time

Location Type

Remote

Department

R&DProductProduct Management

Build a Safer World.

TRM Labs provides AI-powered intelligence solutions that help public and private sector agencies investigate and disrupt crime. TRM's platforms enable investigators to trace illicit activity, build cases, and construct operating pictures of threat networks. Leading agencies and businesses worldwide rely on TRM to make the world safer and more secure.

TRM Labs is building the global standard for investigations.

We're looking for a Product Marketing Manager who understands that this role is not content production. It's market ownership. Your job is to make TRM the obvious choice for a specific set of buyers. You work closely with a Product Manager and Sales — the PM builds, Sales opens doors, and you make sure buyers arrive already convinced. AI handles the execution. You handle the judgment.

Product marketers at TRM make the category feel like TRM's home turf before a buyer ever talks to anyone.

What you'll own

You'll own the market position for TRM's AI-native investigation platform. Your buyers are investigators and analysts running complex, high-stakes cases where the quality of their tooling directly determines outcomes. Your job is to make TRM the platform they can't imagine working without. That means deep fluency with how government investigations actually run, positioning that speaks to the specific workflow pressures these buyers face, and ownership of the moments where TRM cements its position as the standard.

How you'll work

Deep diving: You know the product at the level where you can demo it as well as anyone in the company. You know where the real value sits and where it breaks down. You're in deal reviews and customer conversations often enough to know what lands, and you can hold a real conversation with both engineering and buyers.

Positioning: You find the wedge: the framing where a prospect chooses TRM every time and asking about the competition sounds like the wrong question. You build the architecture everything hangs from: the claims, the proof, the hierarchy, the words TRM owns. Tight enough that a new hire and a ten-year veteran say the same true thing.

Incepting: The story only works if the company believes it first. You get Sales carrying the message without you in the room, engineers who can explain why what they're building matters, and execs who open deals with the same frame you set. You don't mandate alignment. You create it by making the story so clear and compelling that people want to tell it.

Owning the moment: A tier-one launch, a CEO keynote, the webpage a buyer lands on before they ever take a meeting. These are the moments where TRM either makes an impression or misses one. You own the narrative, the timing, and the outcome. The bar is a defining moment the whole company points to. You don't wait for those. You go make them.

What we're looking for

Storytelling. You think in narrative, not slides. You can make something technical matter to a stranger in two sentences. Your stories are grounded in data: win/loss patterns, customer signals, market evidence, because the most persuasive narrative is one that's actually true. You translate the same story across a keynote, a one-pager, and a website without losing what makes it land.

Commercial instincts. You understand what moves a deal, not just what sounds good in a deck. You've been present enough in the sales cycle to know the difference, and you've changed your positioning because of it.

AI builder. You build systems for the team, not just yourself. You've already offloaded the repeatable work to automation: competitive monitoring, content generation, persona synthesis. You spend your time on the judgment calls that actually require you. Walk us through something you built that made the whole team faster.

Judgment. You know what good looks like across the work and you say so when it isn't: a positioning brief that almost works, a website that doesn't land, a design that misses. You hold the standard and give feedback that moves things forward, not feedback that leaves people guessing.

Hard requirements

- 5+ years in product marketing at a B2B SaaS company

- You've owned at least two tier-one launches end to end: strategy, narrative, execution, and post-launch measurement

- You've owned a website or major digital channel and made content decisions that moved pipeline, not just pageviews

- You already use AI to build workflows and systems and can walk through a real example of something you built for your team, not just yourself

Deal breakers

- Marketers who measure output in assets shipped

- Anyone who treats AI as something to explore rather than something already running in their workflow

- Candidates whose best examples inherited existing infrastructure. We need builders, not operators of programs someone else built.

About the team

TRM's product team doesn't coordinate work. It owns outcomes. Product marketers are embedded in the sales motion, in customer conversations, and in launch decisions. The team is small, the scope is real, and what you ship shows up directly in how deals close and how the market talks about TRM. PMMs here don't wait to be asked. If the standard is slipping somewhere, you say so and help. AI is how we work, not just what we build.

What TRM speed looks like in this role

- Build an agent that scans the market for opportunities and builds a prototype for new product features that the product management team reviews

- Customer needs a product brochure before a meeting. You build something on-brand with the right content and get it to them today, without spinning up a design cycle. Fast and accurate does more for the deal than slow and polished.

- Hear the CEO's keynote brief in the morning. Share core message and outline by that afternoon.

The following represents the expected range of compensation for this role:

- Individual pay is determined by skills, qualifications, experience, and location. The compensation details listed in this posting reflect the US base salary only.

- The estimated base salary range for this role is $175,000 - $195,000.

- Additionally, this role may be eligible to participate in TRM’s equity plan.

- Please note – we factor in the different costs for geographies outside the United States.

Our R&D team is distributed not distant and will participate in work weeks, typically 1–2 times per quarter, at a TRM hub or other designated location. Work weeks may be scheduled with as little as 14 days’ notice, and some roles may require additional travel based on team and cross-functional needs. TRM coordinates and covers approved travel, lodging, and workspace. Accommodations are available for legitimate caregiving, health, immigration, and similar

Application Instructions

If you’re interested in joining TRM, we encourage you to apply directly. Every application is reviewed by our Talent team.

Before applying, review the job description carefully and highlight the experience and impact that best demonstrate the required qualifications. Please also provide thoughtful and accurate answers to the application questions, as these will be used to evaluate your skills and qualifications for the role.

If you send your resume directly to someone at TRM, we can’t guarantee it will reach the appropriate hiring team. Applying directly is the best way to ensure your application will be considered.

Interviewing with TRM

Our process is designed to understand how you think, solve problems, and deliver impact, while allowing you to evaluate TRM. Most interview processes include a case study, an AI skills assessment, and a Leadership Principles interview.

- Recruiter Intro: Qualifications, motivations, and alignment with the role.

- Hiring Manager: Deep dive into your relevant experience, skills, and impact.

- First Round: 1–2 interviews focused on the skills most critical to the role.

- Final Round: Hands-on case study. This is usually a panel-style session where we go deeper into your craft, problem-solving, and alignment with TRM.

- References: Former colleagues who can provide insight into your work and impact.

- Offer: Congrats! Your recruiter will present the offer and compensation details.

- Welcome to TRM: We're excited to build a safer world with you!

Your recruiter will share your specific interview plan and preparation guidance along the way.

AI Fluency at TRM

AI fluency is a baseline expectation at TRM.

We believe AI meaningfully changes how top performers operate. We expect every team member to use AI to accelerate and reimagine their craft, not just automate surface tasks.

At TRM, AI fluency means you are among the top 10 percent of operators in your function in how you apply AI to:

- Accelerate repeatable workflows

- Structure and solve problems

- Improve output quality

- Increase speed and leverage

You will be evaluated on applied AI fluency during the interview process.

Life at TRM

We are building a safer world. That promise shows up in how we work every day.

TRM moves FAST. We are a high-velocity, high-ownership team that expects clarity, follow-through, and impact. People who thrive here are energized by hard problems, experimentation, and continuous feedback. If something takes months elsewhere, it will ship here in days.

Our work sits at the intersection of AI, national security, and fighting crime. The problems are complex, the stakes are real, and the environment evolves quickly. The pace and intensity of the work reflect the importance of the mission. As a result, the way we operate requires a high level of ownership, adaptability, collaboration, and creative problem-solving.

At TRM, you should expect:

- Priorities and targets to change quickly

- Operating with a high degree of ambiguity

- A high level of personal ownership and accountability

- Close collaboration across teams and functions

- Frequent, high-touch communication

- Creative problem-solving and out-of-the-box thinking

- A pace that rewards urgency, adaptability, and outcomes

This environment is energizing for people who enjoy building, solving hard problems, and making progress in situations that are not always fully defined. It also requires thriving in ambiguity, adjusting course as new information emerges, and maintaining focus and positivity in a fast-moving and intense environment.

We also recognize that this style of operating is not for everyone. If you are primarily optimizing for predictability or a consistently balanced workload, we encourage you to use the interview process to pressure-test whether this environment is truly the right fit. We want teammates who thrive here, not just survive here.

TRM Labs is looking for an Ecosystem Marketing Lead, Beacon Network to scale TRM's intelligence-sharing network across crypto exchanges, financial institutions, wallet providers, and adjacent compliance and risk teams. Beacon Network is the place these teams come to share scam, fraud, sanctions, and threat signals and to learn from each other. This is a sole-owner growth seat: you set the strategy, run the member acquisition motion, drive the engagement loop, ship the ecosystem marketing program, and report on the metrics that matter. The metrics are active members, signals contributed, signals consumed, and category visibility.

The impact you will have:

- Own the top of the funnel for Beacon Network membership. Set the baseline, the quarterly targets, and the channel mix that lifts active member count across exchanges, FIs, wallet providers, and adjacent compliance / risk teams.

- Own the engagement loop: signals contributed, signals consumed, member-to-member intros, peer roundtables, member-led content. Set the cadence for member success programming (onboarding, monthly value reports, quarterly business reviews).

- Ship Beacon Network's category visibility program: industry events, peer roundtables, partner co-marketing, analyst engagement, and category content. Use AI as default first move for event briefs, content drafting, and partner research.

- Be the single human source of member feedback into the Beacon Network product / partnerships team. Run a weekly product-feedback cycle. Turn the field signal into a roadmap.

- Coordinate with the broader Marketing org on shared community surfaces, including our Compliance Community and LEOLabs, to leverage overlapping audiences and objectives.

- Operate as a one-person team. Brief contractor and AI resources, ship fast, kill what is not working, and report cleanly to Marketing leadership.

What we're looking for:

- 5+ years marketing experience, with at least one role scaling an enterprise member network, industry consortium, or B2B community on a measurable baseline.

- A public-facing track record you can point to: members you acquired, networks you grew, events you ran, communities you built.

— This is not just an email role. It’s a customer loyalty and retention role, with ownership across email, SMS, push notifications, segmentation, automated journeys, loyalty communications, and customer lifetime value.
You’re a lifecycle marketing expert who knows how to build smart, personalized customer journeys that drive retention, loyalty, and revenue. If that sounds like you — and you’re passionate about increasing customer lifetime value, reducing churn, and building marketing that keeps customers engaged for the long haul — you might have what it takes to be our next
CRM Marketing Manager.
Growth opportunity:
This role starts with ownership of our lifecycle marketing engine across email, SMS, push notifications, segmentation, and automated customer journeys. For the right person, there is a clear opportunity to grow into broader leadership across Loyalty, including retention, subscriptions, rewards, customer engagement, and lifetime value. We are looking for someone who can lead the function today and has the potential to grow with it tomorrow.
This job will give you ALL the feels:
At AlgaeCal, we’re driven by a single idea. To end the fear of bone loss. In the United States, an estimated 54 million people have low bone density.
The good news? AlgaeCal has the world’s only clinically-backed natural solution to this problem. We give hope to everyone worried about bone loss. If that excites you, you’ll find no better place to continue your career than at AlgaeCal.
Here’s what you’ll be up to in this busy role:
Leading, coaching, and developing the team — setting a high bar for quality, guiding day-to-day work, and helping people do the best work of their careers.
Creating and managing automations & campaigns that guide customers through every stage of the journey, with a strong focus on increasing retention, loyalty, reorder rate, and customer lifetime value.
Improving how we personalize communications across email, SMS, push, and other owned channels so every touchpoint feels relevant, timely, and effective.
Using data and customer insights to build comprehensive segmentation to make sure the right message reaches the right audience at the right time.
Building, optimizing, and scaling customer journeys in platforms like SFMC, Klaviyo or Braze, while continuously improving performance through testing and iteration.
Overseeing marketing automation performance while helping build and expand other owned channels such as SMS and push notifications.
Overseeing email design and messaging best practices.
This job might be for you if you’ve got…
Experience leading, coaching, or managing a small team, with the ability to set priorities, raise quality, and develop people.

Channel Factory embodies a strong start-up culture that values diversity, collaboration, and results. Our bias toward execution balances critical thinking, analysis, and pragmatic problem-solving. We expect a lot from one another and value our thoughtful, intellectually curious company culture. Remote work status is subject to change at any time.
Channel Factory is headquartered in the United States with global offices across 40+ cities and countries. This position will be based in New York.
We are seeking an exceptional, narrative-driven Sr. Manager, Sales Marketing to lead the strategic storytelling, deck architecture, and go-to-market solution packaging across our commercial organization.
This role sits at the critical intersection of high-level strategy and high-craft visual storytelling. You will be responsible for translating complex adtech capabilities—spanning AI-driven contextual intelligence, multi-platform walled garden activation, dynamic creative optimization, and proprietary suitability data—into punchy, compelling sales narratives and standardized media solutions.
The ideal candidate comes from a high-velocity adtech or digital media background where winning business requires market hustle, strategic differentiation, and the ability to craft category-defining presentations that captivate agency holding companies and enterprise brand marketers.
Key Responsibilities
1. Elite Presentation Crafting & Strategic Narrative Design
Master Storytelling & Deck Architecture: Architect and design high-impact pitch decks, keynotes, and RFP responses with flawless visual flow, executive clarity, and compelling storytelling.
Complexity to Simplicity: Distill technical adtech products into clear, differentiated commercial propositions that arm sellers to win.
Visual Standards: Elevate the standard of visual communication across the sales organization, creating presentation templates that balance clean aesthetic rigor with persuasive narrative arcs.
2. Strategic Media Solutions & GTM Packaging
Verticalized Solutions: Proactively package Channel Factory’s platform capabilities into repeatable, high-margin vertical solutions (e.g., QSR, Auto, CPG, Retail, Entertainment) and seasonal tent-pole opportunities.
Proactive Commercial Strategy: Shift sales marketing from reactive pitch support to proactive market-making by building standardized packages that can be cross-sold across holding company portfolios and independent mid-tier agencies.
Case Studies & Proof Points: Transform campaign performance data and post-campaign wraps into powerful proof-point narratives that demonstrate business impact and drive client retention.
3. Sales Enablement & High-Stakes Client Programs
Strategic Client Programs: Partner directly with sales leadership and brand partnership teams to co-create bespoke collateral for large-scale enterprise proposals, joint business plans (JBPs), and agency upfronts.
Roadshow & Agency Content: Develop content and talk tracks for lunch & learn sessions, executive roadshows, and marketplace education forums.
Seller Toolkits: Build and maintain an intuitive repository of one-sheeters, objection-handling guides, competitive battle-cards, and collateral infused with fresh industry insights.
4. Cross-Functional Collaboration & Market Intelligence
Product & Marketing Bridge: Collaborate closely with Product Marketing, Research, and Regional Marketing teams (US, EMEA, APAC, LATAM) to maintain global narrative alignment while adapting materials for local market realities.
Market Feedback Loop: Gather real-time intelligence from client meetings and the competitive landscape to inform ongoing positioning, research reports, and GTM priorities.
5. Additional Responsibilities
Additional responsibilities and duties as assigned.
Requirements
To be considered for this role, candidates must meet the following criteria:
5-7 years of experience in sales marketing, product marketing, or commercial strategy within the adtech, programmatic, digital media, or agency ecosystem.
World-Class Presentation & Storytelling Portfolio: A proven track record of creating visually stunning, narrative-driven sales decks, keynotes, and client collateral (a portfolio of sample presentations will be requested).
Deep AdTech & Media Domain Expertise: Robust understanding of video advertising, programmatic buying, CTV/OTT, social walled gardens (YouTube, Meta, TikTok), contextual targeting, and brand safety/suitability.
Strategic Packaging Acumen: Demonstrated ability to turn complex tech capabilities and disjointed data points into structured, commercially viable media packages.
High-Velocity Execution: Self-starter mindset capable of managing multiple high-priority deliverables simultaneously in a fast-paced, high-growth environment.
Executive Presence: Strong interpersonal skills to collaborate directly with C-level executives, sales leads, and major agency partners.
Hybrid: minimum of 3 days in office.
Travel: Occasional travel for key client presentations, agency roadshows, team summits, and industry events.
Preferred Qualifications
Experience working inside aggressive, high-growth adtech environments where value-based selling and narrative differentiation are paramount.
Proficiency with modern presentation design tools (Google Slides, PowerPoint, Keynote, Figma) and familiarity with leveraging AI-assisted workflow tools to accelerate collateral production.
Prior experience packaging solutions specifically for key verticals such as Quick Service Restaurants (QSR), Automotive, Consumer Packaged Goods (CPG), or Retail.
Benefits
Work with a leading startup in a high-demand industry, and you would be working with like-minded experts aiming to transform video ad operations
Competitive salary
Comprehensive medical benefits (Medical, Vision, Dental, and Life Insurance)
Cell phone and Wi-Fi reimbursement
Gym Stipend
Bill Spend Stipend
Work-life flexibility – we value your contributions above all
About Channel Factory
Founded in 2010, Channel Factory is an award-winning marketing technology company that helps top global brands and agencies maximize video advertising across YouTube, CTV, and social platforms. Recognized as a technology innovator by Cynopsis and one of the fastest-growing companies by Inc., Channel Factory has served over three hundred of the Fortune 500 in delivering scalable, brand-safe, contextually aligned advertising software and services. By tapping into the deepest proprietary data pool on the market, the company enables highly customized, contextually aware, and dynamically optimized campaigns that deliver industry-leading performance for a portfolio of clients across all sectors.
Channel Factory is an equal-opportunity employer committed to diversity and inclusion in the workplace. We prohibit discrimination and harassment of any kind based on race, color, sex, religion, sexual orientation, national origin, disability, genetic information, pregnancy, or any other protected characteristic as outlined by federal, state, or local laws.
Base Salary Range: $135,000-145,000

Report on MQLs generated, pipeline created and influenced, and conversion to closed-won
Calculate program-level ROI (cost per MQL, cost per pipeline dollar, cost per closed-won customer) and use it to decide what to scale, fix, or cut
Bring a monthly field marketing scorecard to GTM leadership

3-6+ years in field marketing or event marketing ideally at a B2B SaaS company
BA/BS degree or equivalent experience preferred.
A track record of planning and executing trade shows, customer events, and campaigns end to end — not just supporting them
Experience running gifting programs and webinar series as part of a pipeline-generation motion
Comfortable owning a budget and being measured on ROI: MQLs, pipeline sourced/influenced, and conversion to closed-won

Description

100% Remote Position

Base Salary: $70k-$100k

Jump 450 is widely recognized as one of the most elite agencies in customer acquisition and performance media buying. We partner with high-growth brands and operate with a performance-first mindset, holding a high bar for both results and talent. We are seeking experienced Paid Search operators who can step into accounts immediately and drive measurable business impact.

As a Paid Search Associate, you bring strong hands-on experience managing paid search campaigns focused on ecommerce and direct response performance. You are comfortable operating directly in platform, analyzing data, and implementing optimizations that improve revenue, efficiency, and scale. You take ownership of campaign performance and thrive in fast-paced environments where speed, accuracy, and analytical thinking are critical.

In this role, you will work directly with Jump clients and Acquisition Directors to develop and execute testing roadmaps that support aggressive growth targets. You will analyze performance data, identify opportunities for optimization and expansion, and proactively implement changes to ensure campaigns consistently meet or exceed client KPIs.

This role requires someone who is comfortable operating independently in platforms such as Google Ads and Microsoft Ads and has direct experience managing ecommerce campaigns with measurable revenue impact.

Core Responsibilities

- Own day-to-day management and optimization of paid search campaigns across Google Ads and Microsoft Ads
- Build and manage scalable ecommerce account structures including Shopping, Performance Max, brand, and non-brand search campaigns
- Conduct search term analysis and implement negative keyword strategies to reduce wasted spend and improve intent targeting
- Manage and optimize bidding strategies including tROAS, tCPA, Max Conversions, and Max Conversion Value
- Identify opportunities for keyword expansion, match type testing, and campaign scaling while maintaining efficiency targets
- Analyze campaign performance and provide actionable recommendations to improve ROAS, CPA, CVR, and revenue
- Monitor pacing, budgets, and spend allocation across campaigns to ensure efficient growth
- Create clear performance reports and present insights and optimization plans to internal teams and clients

Requirements

- 2–4+ years of hands-on paid search management experience
- Experience managing ecommerce or DTC paid search campaigns with revenue and ROAS goals
- Strong familiarity with Google Ads, Microsoft Ads, and Google Merchant Center
- Experience optimizing Shopping and Performance Max campaigns
- Strong analytical skills and comfort working with large datasets and performance metrics

Benefits

Our Mission

We strive to empower outstanding people to exceed our client’s expectations by providing them with the best resources, merit-based incentives and tools to transform data into actionable insights. Join us on our purpose to provide scalable, strategic and indispensable value to our clients.

About Jump 450

Jump 450, headquartered in New York City, employs top talent globally. Best known for driving exceptional performance outcomes, we’ve scaled numerous companies, and turboscaled 13+ DTC brands from <$100m to 10 figures through data-driven digital advertising and growth hacks.

The record:

1. Acquired by Omnicom ( _NYSE: OMC_) a couple years back
2. Known as the “unicorn maker” tag in PE / VC circles.
3. Driven some crazy numbers ($2bn+ revenue, 400M+ clicks, 40M+ users generated for clients)

Jump manages ~$350mm+ in annual digital media and orchestrates a differentiated agency offering with a focus on: world class creative production, rigorous technical media optimization, customer journey development and robust measurement / analytics–to drive down CAC & extend LTV.

Our standout culture, commitment to employee development, team engagement, and exceptional perks and benefits are some of the reasons why prestigious publications such as Fast Company Magazine, Inc Magazine, and Agency Spotter's Top 30 Agencies 2021, along with Ad Age's Best Places to Work, have featured Jump. Additionally, we are proud to be ranked #899 on the Inc 5000 list and maintain a team member retention rate of over 90% for professional reasons.

What We Offer:

- Competitive salary with performance-based bonuses.
- Health, dental, and vision insurance.
- Paid time off and holidays.
- Opportunities for professional development and career growth.
- A creative and collaborative work environment where your ideas and contributions are valued.
- Additional benefits include

  - Life and Accident Insurance Plans
  - Short and Long Term Disability Plans
  - Employee Assistance Programs
  - Paid Parental Leave
  - Family Forming Plans
  - Cigna Secure Travel
  - Health Savings Account (HDS)
  - Health Care Flexible Spending Account (FSA)
  - Limited Purpose FSA
  - Dependent Care FSA
  - Access to MetLife Legal Plan Services
  - 401k Match Plans
  - Access to Virtual Health Services
  - Remote Working Flexibility
  - Half-Day Fridays
  - New MacBook Pros

Reporting to the Managing Editor in London, you'll manage day-to-day email marketing, retention, and growth campaigns across Who What Wear UK and Marie Claire UK. You'll oversee newsletter scheduling, dedicated brand sends, and third-party partnership campaigns to drive website traffic, affiliate revenue, and subscriber loyalty. What you’ll bring
Demonstrable experience managing email marketing, subscriber segmentation, and automated customer journeys within a digital environment.
Proficiency using Enterprise ESP platforms such as Sailthru, Klaviyo, Selligent, or similar email tools.
Working knowledge of HTML and CSS for email template customization and troubleshooting.
Ability to build custom reports and analyse engagement metrics in Google Analytics.
Experience using project management platforms like Asana, Trello, or Monday.com to coordinate campaign delivery.
Collaborative communication skills with an ability to present performance insights clearly to cross-functional stakeholders.

Experience running multi-stage email marketing campaigns or digital newsletter channels.
Practical experience using ESP software, Google Analytics, and spreadsheet tools like Excel or Google Sheets.
Ability to work from our London office on a hybrid basis.

Discounted rates with Dental care and Private Medical care
When we hit our targets, enjoy a share of our profits with a bonus
Refer a friend scheme - with payment following the successful hire.
Well-being support with access to our Colleague Assistant Programmes

Salary sacrifice Pension scheme up to 5% match
Free drinks and snacks in our offices
