2821.Gecko Job Description: About us: French Florist is a floral boutique reimagining what it means to give and receive flowers. Our handcrafted arrangements are intentionally designed by expert floral designers using only the highest-quality blooms sourced from the best farms around the world. Whether for celebration, connection, or simply delight, our flowers do more than decorate—they elevate and transform moments. With thriving corporate boutiques in Los Angeles and a rapidly expanding franchise network nationwide, French Florist is on a mission to create a more loving and compassionate world through flowers. As purveyors of beauty and connection, we don’t just deliver arrangements—we deliver emotion, meaning, and magic. Role Summary The Paid Media & Acquisition Manager owns day-to-day execution and performance of French Florist's paid media program, Google Ads, Microsoft Ads, and Meta Ads, starting with our corporate boutique accounts. French Florist currently partners with an external paid media agency, but our long-term goal is to bring paid media strategy, execution, optimization, and franchise support in-house. This role will play a central role in that transition—building the internal capabilities, processes, reporting, and playbook needed to create a scalable, high-performing paid media function. This is a hands-on, high-ownership role for a performance marketer who is equally comfortable developing strategy, working directly inside advertising platforms, analyzing performance, reallocating significant budgets, and turning insights into action. You will own paid media performance across corporate and franchise locations, balancing national ecommerce growth with location-level demand generation. You will be responsible for determining where we invest, how we structure campaigns, what we test, and how we scale what works. This role goes beyond campaign management. You will help build the paid acquisition engine that supports French Florist's growth, from campaign architecture and budget allocation to creative testing, measurement, experimentation, landing-page optimization, and market expansion. You will partner closely with the Director of Performance and Growth Marketing, Creative, Product, Ecommerce, CRM, Analytics, and franchise stakeholders to ensure paid media is driving profitable, measurable business growth. We are an AI-first team. Every role at French Florist is built to use AI tools to operate at a scale traditional teams can't. You will use AI to accelerate analysis, campaign development, QA, reporting, creative iteration, research, and experimentation and help build systems and processes that make the entire paid media function more efficient. This is an individual contributor role with significant ownership and autonomy. Success means strong business judgment, rigorous analysis, fast iteration, clean measurement, excellent execution, and the ability to turn performance data into clear decisions. Key Responsibilities 1. Paid Media Strategy & Channel Management Own day-to-day strategy, execution, optimization, and performance across Google Ads, Meta Ads, and Microsoft Ads. Develop and maintain account and campaign architecture that supports both ecommerce growth and location-level demand generation. Own brand and non-brand search, local/location-based campaigns, Shopping, Performance Max, and paid social campaigns. Manage campaign targeting, bidding, budgets, audiences, placements, search terms, product feeds, creative, and other in-platform levers. Continuously identify opportunities to improve acquisition efficiency, increase revenue, and scale profitable demand. Evaluate emerging paid media channels and formats and recommend when and how they should be tested. Build and maintain campaigns for new zip codes, service areas, markets, and store openings. Establish clear test, scale, and kill criteria for campaigns and channels. Ensure paid media strategy reflects seasonality, customer demand, geographic opportunity, inventory, merchandising priorities, and broader business goals. 2. Budget Management, Forecasting & Growth Own paid media budget pacing and allocation across channels, campaigns, and locations. Make in-flight budget decisions based on performance, demand, seasonality, growth opportunity, and expected return. Shift investment toward the highest-value opportunities while maintaining appropriate funding for testing and future growth. Develop paid media forecasts and budget scenarios to support quarterly and annual planning. Recommend where incremental dollars should be invested and identify areas where spend should be reduced or reallocated. Partner with the Director of Performance and Growth Marketing on paid media targets, financial planning, and growth scenarios. Balance short-term efficiency with longer-term customer acquisition and growth objectives. Monitor spend pacing and proactively flag risks, opportunities, and material changes in performance. 3. Creative Strategy & Testing Own the paid-media creative testing roadmap across Meta, Performance Max, and other relevant channels. Identify winning and underperforming creative concepts, hooks, messaging, offers, products, formats, and audiences using performance data. Partner with Creative and Brand teams to translate paid-media insights into actionable creative briefs. Establish a continuous test → learn → iterate process rather than relying solely on periodic creative refreshes. Develop and prioritize creative tests based on expected business impact. Analyze creative performance at the concept, message, format, audience, and placement level. Use AI tools to accelerate creative concepting, copy development, variant generation, analysis, and QA while maintaining French Florist's brand standards. Communicate clear creative learnings back to internal teams so paid media performance informs broader marketing decisions. 4. Testing, Experimentation & Optimization Develop and execute structured experiments across campaigns, audiences, creative, landing pages, products, offers, and channels. Establish clear hypotheses, success metrics, test durations, and decision criteria before launching experiments. Test new keyword categories, audience strategies, campaign types, geographic markets, products, creative concepts, and paid media channels. Partner with Product, Ecommerce, and Creative teams on landing-page and conversion-rate experiments that can improve paid traffic performance. Participate in incrementality, geo, holdout, and other controlled tests when appropriate. Distinguish between correlation and causation when evaluating campaign performance. Document learnings and turn successful experiments into repeatable playbooks. Continuously challenge existing assumptions and identify opportunities to improve the paid acquisition system. 5. Measurement, Attribution & Analytics Own paid media performance reporting and translate raw data into clear business insights and recommendations. Use GA4, Google Ads, Meta Ads, Microsoft Ads, server-side tracking, and third-party attribution tools to evaluate performance. Monitor discrepancies between advertising platforms, GA4, attribution systems, and business revenue data. Identify tracking gaps, attribution issues, and measurement inconsistencies and proactively work with internal teams to resolve them. Use ROAS, MER, CAC, CPA, conversion rate, revenue, contribution margin, and other relevant metrics to evaluate performance. Incorporate customer lifetime value and customer quality into acquisition decisions. Evaluate prospecting versus retention investment and make recommendations based on customer value. Partner with the Director of Performance and Growth Marketing on measurement infrastructure, including GA4, GTM, server-side tracking, and conversion APIs. Develop clear performance narratives that explain not only what happened, but why it happened and what we should do next. Use AI tools to accelerate reporting, anomaly detection, data analysis, and performance insights. 6. Landing Pages, Ecommerce & Conversion Optimization Partner with Product, CRO, Creative, and Development teams to improve landing pages and onsite experiences that receive paid traffic. Identify site friction and conversion opportunities using paid media performance data. Provide paid-media requirements and feedback for new product pages, location pages, category pages, and website launches. Evaluate landing-page performance by campaign, market, product, audience, and traffic source. Partner on CRO testing involving CTAs, product presentation, messaging, photography, trust signals, offers, and other conversion drivers. Ensure paid campaigns and landing pages are aligned in terms of intent, messaging, geography, products, and customer experience. Act as the paid media point of contact during major website changes, launches, and migrations. Maintain campaign/URL mappings and execute paid-media QA checklists for site changes. 7. Local & Franchise Growth Own paid media strategy across corporate and franchise locations as the network expands. Serve as the primary day-to-day paid media partner for franchise owners. Translate campaign performance into clear, actionable recommendations for individual locations. Identify market-level opportunities based on search demand, geography, budget, competition, seasonality, and performance. Develop scalable frameworks for launching and managing paid media across new franchise locations. Guide new franchise owners through paid media launches and establish expectations around budget, timing, performance, and market conditions. Explain performance shifts and trade-offs to franchise owners in clear, non-technical language. Gather franchise feedback and translate recurring needs into improvements to paid media processes and systems. Develop reporting and communication processes that can scale as the franchise network grows. Maintain consistency in paid media strategy while allowing for market-specific optimization. 8. AI & Operational Excellence Use AI tools such as Claude and other emerging technologies to accelerate campaign development, analysis, reporting, QA, research, creative iteration, and documentation. Build repeatable AI-assisted workflows that improve speed and quality without sacrificing strategic judgment. Use automation where appropriate to reduce manual campaign management and reporting. Continuously identify opportunities to improve paid media processes, documentation, and operating systems. Establish clear test, scale, and kill criteria for campaigns and channels. Budget Management, Forecasting & Growth Own paid media budget pacing and allocation across channels, campaigns, and locations. Make in-flight budget decisions based on performance, demand, seasonality, growth opportunity, and expected return. Shift investment toward the highest-value opportunities while maintaining appropriate funding for testing and future growth. Develop paid media forecasts and budget scenarios to support quarterly and annual planning. Recommend where incremental dollars should be invested and identify areas where spend should be reduced or reallocated. Partner with the Director of Performance and Growth Marketing on paid media targets, financial planning, and growth scenarios. Balance short-term efficiency with longer-term customer acquisition and growth objectives. Monitor spend pacing and proactively flag risks, opportunities, and material changes in performance. 3. Creative Strategy & Testing Own the paid-media creative testing roadmap across Meta, Performance Max, and other relevant channels. Identify winning and underperforming creative concepts, hooks, messaging, offers, products, formats, and audiences using performance data. Partner with Creative and Brand teams to translate paid-media insights into actionable creative briefs. Establish a continuous test → learn → iterate process rather than relying solely on periodic creative refreshes. Develop and prioritize creative tests based on expected business impact. Analyze creative performance at the concept, message, format, audience, and placement level. Use AI tools to accelerate creative concepting, copy development, variant generation, analysis, and QA while maintaining French Florist's brand standards. Communicate clear creative learnings back to internal teams so paid media performance informs broader marketing decisions. 4. Testing, Experimentation & Optimization Develop and execute structured experiments across campaigns, audiences, creative, landing pages, products, offers, and channels. Establish clear hypotheses, success metrics, test durations, and decision criteria before launching experiments. Test new keyword categories, audience strategies, campaign types, geographic markets, products, creative concepts, and paid media channels. Partner with Product, Ecommerce, and Creative teams on landing-page and conversion-rate experiments that can improve paid traffic performance. Participate in incrementality, geo, holdout, and other controlled tests when appropriate. Distinguish between correlation and causation when evaluating campaign performance. Document learnings and turn successful experiments into repeatable playbooks. Continuously challenge existing assumptions and identify opportunities to improve the paid acquisition system. 5. Measurement, Attribution & Analytics Own paid media performance reporting and translate raw data into clear business insights and recommendations. Use GA4, Google Ads, Meta Ads, Microsoft Ads, server-side tracking, and third-party attribution tools to evaluate performance. Monitor discrepancies between advertising platforms, GA4, attribution systems, and business revenue data. Identify tracking gaps, attribution issues, and measurement inconsistencies and proactively work with internal teams to resolve them. Use ROAS, MER, CAC, CPA, conversion rate, revenue, contribution margin, and other relevant metrics to evaluate performance. Use AI tools to accelerate reporting, anomaly detection, data analysis, and performance insights. 6. Identify site friction and conversion opportunities using paid media performance data. Translate campaign performance into clear, actionable recommendations for individual locations. Identify market-level opportunities based on search demand, geography, budget, competition, seasonality, and performance. Develop scalable frameworks for launching and managing paid media across new franchise locations. Guide new franchise owners through paid media launches and establish expectations around budget, timing, performance, and market conditions. Build repeatable AI-assisted workflows that improve speed and quality without sacrificing strategic judgment. Use automation where appropriate to reduce manual campaign management and reporting. 2822.Gecko Job Description: Job Description As a Senior Paid Search Analyst, you will lead the management and optimization of advanced paid search campaigns across platforms like Google Ads and Bing Ads, driving ROI and traffic through strategic, data-driven approaches. You will analyze performance metrics, implement optimizations, conduct A/B testing, and collaborate with account managers and clients to align campaigns with business goals. In addition to managing complex budgets and ensuring quality, you will mentor junior analysts, conduct QA, and facilitate cross-departmental training. With a focus on innovation and staying ahead of industry trends, you will play a critical role in delivering competitive, cutting-edge paid search solutions. Job Responsibilities: Plan, execute, and optimize paid search campaigns based on client goals and objectives. Direct management of 20-30 automotive paid search accounts, with individual budgets ranging from $25k-$150k per account per month. Collaborate closely with account managers on strategy, provide campaign performance and recommend opportunities for improvement. Maintain performance standards on all assigned accounts Monitor Budget Pacing, Conversion Tracking, and Traffic Quality Monitor and analyze campaign performance such as click-through rate (CTR), conversion rate, and return on ad spend (ROAS) to identify opportunities for optimization and improvement. Test products to determine propensity to drive positive results. Generate regular reports to track campaign performance and communicate key findings. Stay up to date on the latest industry trends, best practices to ensure our paid search strategies remain cutting-edge and competitive. Facilitate Training for Associate Paid Search Analysts and Paid Search Analysts Mentorship for New Paid Search Analysts QA accounts for other members of the Paid Search Team Oversight and Troubleshooting on Paid Search Accounts Manage Portfolio wide performance and benchmarking Facilitating cross departmental relationships and cross departmental trainings Conducting A/B tests and developing new strategies or tools Presenting Data To other departments Required Qualifications: Minimum 3-5 years of experience with paid search campaign management Experience and strong understanding of PPC advertising Experience using industry tools such as Google Analytics, Google Adwords, SA360, etc. Understand paid media advertising budget management and effective, data-driven ad spend. Ability to analyze data sets and identify trends based on industry KPIs. Ability to work independently and collaboratively in a fast-paced, deadline-driven environment. Exceptional written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to articulate complex ideas clearly and concisely. Strong quantitative, analytical skills and attention to detail with the ability to interpret data and actionable insights. Excellent time-management and organizational skills Proficient in Microsoft Office/Google Workspace (Docs, Sheets, Slides, GMail, GChat) Focuses on strategic planning and execution of campaigns aligned with client goals, using data-driven insights to optimize performance. Demonstrates mentorship and leadership skills with experience in training and guiding junior team members. Comprehensive, up-to-date understanding of industry trends, best practices, and emerging paid search tools to drive competitive strategies. Demonstrates strong attention to detail in QA of paid search accounts while effectively troubleshooting and resolving campaign performance or setup issues. Proficiency in managing and optimizing paid search campaigns across platforms such as Google Ads and Bing Ads, with expertise in budget pacing, conversion tracking, traffic quality metrics, A/B testing, and performance analysis to identify optimization opportunities. Demonstrates excellent communication skills to collaborate with account managers, departments, and clients, with experience presenting campaign data, insights, and recommendations to Account Managers and clients. Preferred Qualifications: Agency experience Experience in automotive Bachelor’s degree in Marketing, Business, Data Analytics, ISDS, or equivalent experience Google Certifications (Google Analytics, Google Ads)

2823.FireCrawl Job Description: The Manager of Marketing, Paid Search owns the strategy, performance, and team responsible for paid search at Strayer University (SU). Reporting directly to the Director of Media Investments, this role is accountable for a multi-million dollar channel budget, for translating enrollment and revenue targets into forecasts and bid strategy, and for leading a team of paid search professionals. The Manager serves as the organization’s subject matter expert on search as the channel shifts toward AI-driven campaign types and automated bidding, sets and documents the channel standards and playbooks used across the Media Investments paid search function, and prepares the team and the channel operating model to absorb adjacent biddable channels should they be brought in-house in 2027. The position collaborates with teams across the marketing organization, including Media Strategy, Marketing Analytics, Marketing Operations, Digital Experiences, Brand, and Product Portfolio Marketing. Essential Duties & Responsibilities: Owns end-to-end paid search strategy for Strayer University, translating enrollment and revenue targets into channel goals, budget allocation, and bid strategy across brand and non-brand Accountable for a multi-million dollar annual paid search budget, including forecast development, in-quarter pacing, reallocation decisions, and defending spend and performance recommendations to Media Strategy, Finance, and business leadership Owns the multi-quarter paid search roadmap and test-and-learn agenda; prioritizes initiatives based on enrollment impact rather than channel-level efficiency alone Makes and defends independent channel decisions within approved budget and performance guardrails; escalates to the Director only where decisions carry cross-brand or enterprise consequences Serves as enterprise subject matter expert on paid search; authors points of view on platform changes, forced migrations, and emerging campaign types, and recommends an enterprise position to the Director Directs campaign architecture and ongoing management, including new builds, restructures, match type and audience strategy, budget changes, bid adjustments, and ad copy, ensuring industry, brand, and legal compliance Sets strategy for automated and AI-driven campaign types, including Performance Max, AI Max for Search, and value-based and portfolio bidding; exercises judgment on when to rely on platform automation and when to override it Owns signal quality as a primary performance lever, including conversion definitions, offline conversion imports, value rules, audience feeds, and first-party data inputs, in partnership with Marketing Analytics and Marketing Operations Accountable for the configuration, governance, and return on investment of the paid search bid management platform and related channel technology; evaluates and recommends platform renewals and changes Directs the creation, automation, and maintenance of SEM reporting and analytics; partners with Marketing Analytics on standardized dashboards and on incrementality and geo-holdout testing to validate channel contribution Accountable for lead quality outcomes in addition to volume; partners with Enrollment, Marketing Operations, and Marketing Analytics to connect CPL and CPA to downstream application, start, and persistence metrics Manages, develops, and retains a team of one to five paid search professionals; sets goals, delivers regular feedback and formal performance reviews, and builds individual development plans Establishes and documents channel standards, quality assurance protocols, and playbooks for the paid search function; partners with peer channel leaders to drive consistent adoption across Media Investments Accountable for contribution to a positive, inclusive team culture and for the professional growth of team members beyond direct reports Owns day-to-day relationships with Google, Microsoft, and other search partners; leads quarterly business reviews, secures support and co-op resources, and escalates enterprise-level commitments to the Director Presents channel performance, forecasts, and strategic recommendations to senior marketing stakeholders and executives on a monthly and quarterly cadence Partners with Media Strategy, Product Portfolio Marketing, and Brand teams to ensure alignment on objectives, program priorities, launch timing, and messaging Advocates for paid search landing experience and site needs with the Digital Experiences team; partners with Marketing Operations to troubleshoot lead management and tracking issues Assesses team and operating-model readiness for adjacent biddable channels targeted for in-housing in 2027, such as paid social and display or programmatic; scopes resourcing, technology, and training requirements and recommends a transition plan to the Director, who owns the enterprise capability roadmap Monitors competitive and industry trends, including the evolving role of AI-generated search experiences, and informs relevant stakeholders of implications for strategy and investment Job Skills: Expert-level proficiency in paid search strategy, with demonstrated ability to own a channel budget and defend forecast and investment recommendations to senior leadership Strong quantitative and analytical skills; able to build and pressure-test forecasts, size opportunities, and design statistically valid tests Fluency in automated bidding and AI-driven campaign types, with sound judgment about when to rely on platform automation and when to intervene Proven people leadership; able to hire, develop, and retain talent and to deliver direct, actionable feedback Effective communicator and presenter; can translate complex, technical search concepts into a clear business narrative for executive audiences Ability to influence without authority across analytics, operations, creative, brand, and product partners Sound decision making under ambiguity in a fast-paced, constantly evolving environment Meticulous attention to detail, paired with the discipline to prioritize at the portfolio level Ability to manage work across multiple internal and external partners simultaneously Advanced Excel user Certification or experience with enterprise search bid management platforms, particularly Skai (Kenshoo) Advanced user of Google Ads and Microsoft Advertising UI and Editor tools Working proficiency in GA4 and in data visualization tools such as Tableau, Power BI, or Looker Studio Google Ads certifications preferred Work Experience: 6+ years’ experience focused on PPC/SEM responsibilities, including a minimum of 2 years of direct people leadership. Experience managing paid search in a regulated, lead generation, or considered-purchase category preferred; higher education experience is a plus. Education: Bachelor Degree, MBA preferred. Other: Must be able to travel 10% of time. Must be able to lift 15 lbs. Typical office setting. Mobility within the office including movement from floor to floor. Travel via plane, car, and metro may be required to perform this job. Must be able to work more than 40 hours per week when business needs warrant Access information using a computer. Effectively communicate, both up and down the management chain. Effectively cope with stressful situations. Strong mental acuity. Regular, dependable attendance and punctuality are essential functions of this job. Other essential functions and marginal job functions are subject to modification. SEI offers a comprehensive package of benefits to employees scheduled 30 hours or more per week. In addition to medical, dental, vision, life and disability plans, SEI employees may take advantage of well-being incentives, parental leave, paid time off, certain paid holidays, tax saving accounts (FSA, HSA), 401(k) retirement benefit, Employee Stock Purchase Plan, tuition assistance as well as entertainment and retail discounts. Non-exempt employees are eligible for overtime pay, if applicable. We strive to attract talent with broad experiences, skills and perspectives. We welcome applications from all. While it is not typical for an individual to be hired at or near the top end of the pay range at SEI, we offer a competitive salary. The actual base pay offered to the successful candidate may vary depending on multiple factors including, but not limited to, job-related knowledge/skills, experience, business needs, geographical location, and internal pay equity. Our Talent Acquisition Team is ready to discuss your interest in joining SEI. The expected salary range for this position is below. $95,100.00 - $142,600.00 - Salary If you require reasonable accommodations to complete our application process, please contact our Human Resources Department at Careers@strategiced.com .

2824.FireCrawl Job Description: About Us We're a Boca Raton-based digital marketing agency with more than a decade in the industry, focused on behavioral health, mental health, addiction treatment and senior living. We help treatment providers compete in a market dominated by large operators with big budgets, and we do it with data-driven decisions, not overblown promises. Paid search is at the core of what we deliver, supported by our SEO, web development, and call tracking and dashboarding teams. About the Role We're hiring a Director of Paid Search with deep, hands-on Google Ads expertise to lead PPC performance across our client accounts. You'll own search end to end: structure, bidding, tracking, testing, budget and reporting. Success is measured by qualified calls, admissions and cost per acquisition, not clicks. This is a search role, not a social media role. Responsibilities Own Google Ads strategy and performance across multiple client accounts, with Microsoft Advertising as a secondary channel. Build scalable account structures by service line, level of care, location and payer focus. Get the most out of every client budget so clients can compete against larger operators. Manage Search and Performance Max campaigns, and keep PMax from cannibalizing branded search. Lead keyword research, search term mining and negative keyword management in high-cost, highly competitive healthcare verticals. Write and test ad copy that complies with Google's healthcare and addiction-services policies and client LegitScript requirements. Manage Smart Bidding strategies optimized toward qualified calls and admissions, not raw leads. Own conversion tracking across GA4, Google Tag Manager and call conversions. Integrate call tracking data from CallTrackingMetrics and CallRail into campaign optimization and client dashboards. Partner with our SEO and web development teams on landing page performance and conversion rate optimization. Run A/B tests on ads and landing pages. Manage client ad budgets: pace spend, forecast CPA and explain variances. Give clients honest, data-backed reporting and set realistic expectations. Support and develop paid search team members. Requirements 4+ years of hands-on Google Ads experience. Has managed Google Ads accounts independently, from build through optimization. Solid understanding of Smart Bidding, Performance Max and keyword strategy. Working knowledge of GA4 and Google Tag Manager. Experience setting up and auditing conversion and call tracking. Track record of improving CPA or campaign performance. Strong Excel/Google Sheets skills. Comfortable presenting results directly to clients. Preferred Behavioral health, addiction treatment, mental health or senior living advertising experience. Familiarity with Google's addiction-services ad policy and LegitScript certification. 2825.FireCrawl Job Description: About the Role Riverside Mental Health is seeking an experienced, strategic, and results-driven Marketing Manager to lead marketing efforts across our growing network of behavioral health practices. This is a hands-on leadership role responsible for developing and executing marketing strategies that increase brand awareness, generate qualified client leads, strengthen referral pipelines, and support sustainable growth across multiple clinics and markets. The Marketing Manager will oversee marketing strategy, execution, analytics, and optimization across digital and traditional channels while working closely with Riverside leadership and individual clinic teams. The ideal candidate can think strategically at the organizational level while also being comfortable getting into the details and executing campaigns. Success in this position will be measured not simply by marketing activity, but by measurable growth in qualified leads, client acquisition, referral sources, and return on marketing investment. Key Responsibilities Marketing Strategy & Growth Develop and execute a comprehensive marketing strategy across Riverside Mental Health and its affiliated practices. Create market-specific strategies based on each clinic's services, specialties, geography, and growth objectives. Make data-driven recommendations on Marketing resource decisions, including insource/outsource decisions Effectively manage and grow a small team of marketing employees and contractors Balance short-term lead generation with long-term brand development and market positioning. Identify new opportunities, channels, partnerships, and initiatives to support organizational growth. Establish clear marketing goals, KPIs, and performance benchmarks. Lead Generation & Client Acquisition Develop and manage multi-channel campaigns designed to generate qualified client inquiries and consultations. Optimize inbound, outbound, digital, and referral marketing channels to improve conversion. Evaluate and test new lead-generation opportunities and referral sources. Work with clinic leadership and intake teams to understand lead quality, conversion rates, clinician capacity, and areas of greatest need. Use performance data to continuously improve client acquisition strategies. Digital Marketing & Paid Advertising Manage and optimize paid advertising campaigns across Google Ads, Meta, and other relevant platforms. Oversee campaign targeting, creative, budgets, bidding strategies, and performance. Monitor cost per lead, conversion rates, ROI, and other key performance indicators. Continually test and refine campaigns to improve results and marketing efficiency. Content, SEO & Brand Management Oversee website, SEO, social media, email marketing, and content strategy across Riverside and its practices. Develop content that supports search visibility, client engagement, and lead generation. Collaborate with clinicians and leadership to translate clinical expertise into accessible, compelling marketing content. Maintain consistent brand standards while preserving the individual identity and market positioning of each practice. Ensure marketing materials appropriately reflect the sensitivity and ethical considerations of behavioral healthcare marketing. Referral & Community Marketing Develop strategies to strengthen professional referral networks and community partnerships. Support outreach to physicians, schools, healthcare providers, therapists, community organizations, and other referral partners. Identify opportunities for community engagement, partnerships, events, and other relationship-based marketing initiatives. Track referral sources and evaluate the effectiveness of outreach efforts. Analytics, Reporting & Budget Management Establish and maintain reliable tracking across websites, advertising platforms, CRM systems, analytics tools, and other marketing channels. Monitor marketing performance across individual clinics and the organization as a whole. Provide regular reporting to executive leadership with clear analysis, recommendations, and next steps. Manage marketing budgets and allocate resources based on performance and organizational priorities. Track ROI and make timely, data-driven adjustments to improve performance. Qualifications Demonstrated experience developing and executing successful marketing strategies. Strong experience with lead generation, digital marketing, paid advertising, SEO, content strategy, and marketing analytics. Experience managing Google Ads, Meta advertising, and other digital marketing platforms. Strong analytical skills with the ability to translate marketing data into actionable business decisions. Experience managing marketing budgets and measuring ROI. Ability to manage marketing initiatives across multiple brands, locations, or markets. Excellent project management, organizational, and communication skills. Ability to work independently and take ownership of projects from strategy through execution. Experience in mental health, behavioral health, healthcare, or another healthcare-related industry strongly preferred. Understanding of the privacy, ethical, and reputational considerations involved in healthcare marketing. Bachelor's degree in Marketing, Communications, Business, or a related field preferred, or equivalent professional experience. What We're Looking For We are looking for someone who is both a strategist and a doer. This person should be able to identify where Riverside should invest its marketing resources, build the strategy, execute or coordinate the work, measure the results, and change course when the data calls for it. The right candidate will be comfortable operating in a growing organization where individual practices have different needs and markets, while building a cohesive marketing strategy that supports Riverside Mental Health as a whole. Compensation: $110,000 - 125,000 per year Riverside Mental Health is an equal opportunity employer. Pay: $110,000.00 - $125,000.00 per year Benefits: 401(k) 401(k) matching Flexible schedule Health insurance Retirement plan Work Location: Remote

2826.Gecko Job Description: At BairesDev®, we've been leading the way in technology projects for over 15 years. We deliver cutting-edge solutions to giants like Google and the most innovative startups in Silicon Valley. Our diverse 4,000+ team, composed of the world's Top 1% of tech talent, works remotely on roles that drive significant impact worldwide. When you apply for this position, you're taking the first step in a process that goes beyond the ordinary. We aim to align your passions and skills with our vacancies, setting you on a path to exceptional career development and success. Head of Solutions Marketing at BairesDev In this role, you'll build and lead a new Customer Marketing area from the ground up, reporting directly to the CMO. This is a hands-on leadership position where you'll turn our existing client base and our sales collateral into a genuine growth lever for the company. This is your opportunity to inherit an experienced team of about eight people across three functions, define the strategy yourself, and work with executives across Sales, Client Engagement, Delivery, and Marketing from day one. What You'll Do: Own product marketing hands-on, defining positioning and messaging for go-to-market plans for our service lines and new offerings, and maintaining competitive intelligence on competitors. Lead the Sales Collateral and Copywriting teams, setting the positioning and messaging frameworks briefing and quality standards, and delivering pitch decks, case studies, one-pagers, and proposals that Sales measurably uses. Lead Customer Marketing and Events, building upsell and cross-sell campaigns, executive events, client references, and advocacy programs with revenue targets agreed with Sales and Client Engagement. Build the new area by hiring, defining KPIs such as collateral adoption by Sales, influenced pipeline, and revenue from existing accounts, and reporting results to the CMO and executive team. Partner with Sales leadership to identify win-rate gaps by segment and close them through messaging, collateral, and enablement. What we are looking for: 8+ years of overall B2B marketing experience, including 4+ years in a leadership role. 3+ years of hands-on experience as a Product Marketing Manager or Director, owning positioning, messaging, and launches at a B2B company. Bachelor's degree in Marketing, Business, Communications, Economics, or Engineering. Experience in customer marketing, including upsell/cross-sell campaigns, client case studies and references, client events and webinars, and ABM to existing accounts. Proficiency in copy management, including briefing, editing, and quality control of B2B copy, and managing writers. Nice to have: Background in IT services, nearshore software outsourcing, or IT staffing (e.g., Globant, EPAM, Endava, Toptal, Thoughtworks, Accenture). Experience building a marketing function or team from zero inside a company of 1,000+ employees. Prior experience reporting directly to a CMO or sitting on an executive leadership team. How we make your work (and your life) easier: 100% remote work. Work-from-home hardware setup. Flexible hours, make your schedule. PTO, parental leave, and other special leaves. An excellent compensation package, well above market average. Healthcare coverage (Vision and Dental). Life Insurance. 401K Plan. Diverse and multicultural work environment. Collaborate and learn from the global Top 1% of talent in each area. Supportive environment with mentorship, promotions, skill development, and diverse growth opportunities. Join a global team where your unique talents can truly thrive and make a significant impact! Apply now!

2827.FireCrawl Job Description: Butler/Till is a results-driven marketing agency offering deeply collaborative client experiences, proprietary technology, and world-class partnerships. SUMMARY The Paid Search Strategist at Butler/Till supports small business clients by combining hands-on paid search execution with consultative client support. This role balances campaign management, reporting, and optimization with educating clients on how paid search drives their business goals. As a subject matter expert, the Strategist analyzes performance, ensures quality, supports strategy and planning, and optimizes KPIs while collaborating closely with internal teams and staying current on industry trends. KEY OUTCOMES & RESPONSIBILITIES Key Outcome: Client Support and Education Key Responsibilities: Serve as an expert point of contact for clients enrolled in our Paid Search program Educate clients on paid search fundamentals and program details Provide performance read outs and insights, showcasing how our team’s work drives business outcomes Coach clients on appropriate budget and investment level Maintain documentation of client communication Key Outcome: Measurement and Reporting Key Responsibilities: Analyze, review, and report on effectiveness of campaigns to clients Effectively communicates and educates internal teams on performance nuances, citing team-driven optimizations and/or external factors that impacted performance Acts as channel SME, fields any questions and/or provide any follow-ups to channel-specific inquiries May be asked to assist with troubleshooting of reporting and/or trafficking mapping and/or site tagging to assist with campaign measurement Collaborates with Analytics to ensure data accuracy in dashboards and recommend appropriate KPIs for recommended channel activation strategies Collaborates with channel peers to understand cross-channel dependencies and build synergistic strategies to further overall campaign performance Translate raw performance data into clear, meaningful stories about campaign results Use data-driven insights to optimize and improve paid media performance Partner with clients to drive progress toward their business goals Key Outcome: Planning and Strategy Key Responsibilities Collaborate with cross-functional teams to gather insights, offer recommendations and optimizations to exceed campaign benchmarks and client business objectives Continuously analyze key performance metrics to measure effectiveness of campaign initiatives Support in identifying testing opportunities quarterly, contributing to testing briefs, recommendations, and execution plans Work with Senior Specialists to prepare materials like POVs and other thought leadership to educate internal and client stakeholders on strategy shifts, account restructuring, etc. Key Outcome: Communication & Collaboration Key Responsibilities: Act as a bridge between the Paid Search team and client needs, concerns, and perspectives Support the Planning team in developing channel plans, including budget forecasts, campaign and bid strategies, account structure, competitive insights, testing opportunities, and actionable learnings Collaborate with Analytics, Planning, and Account Service teams to develop reporting and craft clear, effective client communications Partner cross-functionally to author thought leadership materials, including POVs, blog posts, white papers, and speaking content QUALIFICATIONS Required Bachelor’s degree in Marketing, Advertising, Communications, Business or equivalent work experience Minimum of 3 years of experience managing and leading campaigns in the channel ecosystem Experience with strategic planning and applied experience of bringing plans to execution Proven track record in operating with a high-level of integrity, commitment, and enthusiasm to take on a challenging role with cross-functional commitments Preferred Experience working in multi-location marketing and/or highly regulated industries Proactive and curious attitude Strong problem-solving skills Comfortable operating in a fast-paced, deadline driven environment with rapidly changing priorities Use of advanced Search bidding platforms (SA360, Marin, etc.) Strong Excel skills (VLOOKUP, Pivot tables/charts, etc.) Experience in customer-facing roles about paid media performance and strategy CORE COMPETENCIES CUSTOMER FOCUS/CLIENT INTIMACY: Seeking to understand client business challenges/needs and delivering continuous value to our clients COLLABORATIVE: Working with teams and across the organization with ease OWNER AGILITY: Able to continuously learn and quickly adapt to changing circumstance RESULTS DRIVEN: Accepts accountability to deliver business outcomes, even under changing circumstances. Additional travel is not routinely expected but may be required for key/critical meetings & events. WORK ENVIORNMENT & PHYSICAL DEMANDS The work environment and physical demands characteristics described here are representative of those an employee encounters while performing the essential functions of this job, typically in an office setting or in a home office. An employee in this role may be in a stationary position, often standing or sitting for prolonged periods and using office equipment and computers. The noise level in the office environment is usually moderate (i.e., business office with computers and printers, light foot traffic, etc.). This applies to all terms and conditions of employment, including recruiting, hiring, placement, promotion, termination, layoff, recall, transfer, leaves of absence, compensation, and training. COMPENSATION Butler/Till is committed to providing pay transparency of our compensation philosophy and ensuring equitable pay practices for our employee owners. The compensation range for this position is $49,000- $72,000 and represents the annual salary range in Rochester, NY. Base pay offered may vary depending on multiple individualized factors, including location, skills, and experience. This is just one component of Butler/Till’s total compensation package for employee owners. The total compensation package for this position may also include other elements, including ESOP (employee stock ownership plan), an annual bonus, in addition to a full benefits package, and paid time off benefits, including 100% paid parental leave. Details of participation in these benefit plans will be provided if an employee receives an offer of employment.

2828.Gecko Job Description: Location : Remote About the Role The Assistant Director, Paid Search leads paid search strategy and day-to-day work across Google Search, Performance Max, and ChatGPT Ads for a group of complex Carnegie clients. You’ll also manage and coach 1–3 paid search team members. You’ll work closely with the Directors and Senior Director of Paid Search to support high-stakes client work, grow the team, and shape how Carnegie approaches AI-driven search. What You’ll Own Paid Search Strategy & Execution Run paid search strategy and execution from start to finish for a portfolio of complex, high-spend clients. Manage and optimize Google Ads campaigns, using paid search best practices to drive results. Troubleshoot complex PPC issues on your own before escalating. Track account performance using down-funnel goals and CRM data where available, and use what you find to shape recommendations. Use Google Analytics, Carnegie Clarity, Profound, and other reporting tools to spot opportunities. Build and review client-facing campaign build-outs, recommendations, and other materials that turn strategy into clear next steps. Partner with Digital Strategists and other teams on the paid search pieces of proposals, RFPs, and strategic initiatives. Client Leadership Serve as the trusted paid search advisor and main point of contact for your clients. Lead client conversations with confidence and build strong relationships. Present strategy, performance insights, recommendations, and campaign changes to clients, including on larger and more complex accounts. Learn each client’s goals and turn them into paid search strategies that support their broader objectives. Team Leadership & Development Manage and develop 1–3 paid search team members with ongoing coaching, feedback, and support. Lead training and onboarding, and help build team resources and best practices. Give regular performance feedback and contribute to formal performance reviews. Act as a senior resource for the team, helping others sharpen their technical PPC and client management skills. AI Search & Innovation Guide campaign strategy through the shifting AI-driven search landscape, using automation and new capabilities to improve performance. Stay current on Google Ads and AI search developments, and find ways to put new capabilities to work for clients. Help shape Carnegie’s paid search approach to AI search by testing new ideas, sharing what you learn, and building best practices for the team. Team Knowledge & Thought Leadership Share knowledge and best practices with teammates and cross-functional partners. Contribute to paid search training, process improvements, and team initiatives. Stay on top of industry trends and bring new ideas to the team. What You Bring 3–6 years of hands-on paid search experience, with strong Google Ads expertise and experience managing complex, high-spend campaigns. Strong technical grasp of Google Ads strategy, optimization, and performance management. Experience directly managing at least one team member, including coaching, feedback, and day-to-day leadership. Strong client-facing communication skills, and the confidence to lead meetings, present recommendations, and build relationships. Experience creating detailed client-facing campaign build-outs, strategic recommendations, and presentations. Strong attention to detail, and the ability to turn strategy into clear, workable campaign execution. Experience analyzing digital campaign metrics to measure success. Strong problem-solving skills, plus the ability to troubleshoot issues and pick up new tools and technologies quickly. A forward-thinking approach to paid search, and openness to testing and adopting new Google Ads and AI search capabilities. Professional presence, and the ability to communicate well with clients, colleagues, and senior stakeholders. Strong team player with excellent time management, able to juggle multiple priorities in a remote environment. A plus: experience with Enhanced Conversions for Leads (ECL), Google Tag Gateway (GTG), AI Max, ChatGPT Ads, or other emerging ad capabilities. A plus: lead generation experience. A plus: experience with Asana or similar project management tools, and Google Docs, Sheets, and Slides. Why This Role Paid search is changing fast, and this role puts you at the center of it. You’ll run strategy for clients that matter, grow the people on your team, and help decide how Carnegie uses AI-driven search. You’ll see your impact in client results and in the skills of the people you coach. Compensation The salary range for this role is $85,000–$95,000. Your offer will reflect the experience, skills, and qualifications you bring. About Carnegie For more than 30 years, Carnegie has been a leader and innovator in higher education marketing and enrollment strategy, offering groundbreaking services in the areas of Research, Strategy, Digital Marketing, Lead Generation, Slate Optimization, Student Search, Website Development, and Creative that generate authentic connections. No phone calls or unscheduled visits to the office, please. Carnegie is an equal-opportunity employer.

This role may become eligible for discretionary bonus, commission, and/or equity compensation after an initial period in the role, at the Company's sole discretion. Eligibility, timing, and amounts are not guaranteed and are not part of the base offer. Benefits: Unlimited PTO, major U.S. holidays observed, and health, dental, and vision insurance options available. ABOUT INFINITE OUTDOORS Infinite Outdoors is a private land hunting and fishing access platform, working alongside its subsidiary Access Granted to expand outdoor recreation access. 2833.FireCrawl Job Description:
Job Title - Specialist, Performance Marketing

This position is also known as: Paid Search Manager, Paid Search Specialist; SEM Specialist; Performance Marketing Specialist; Digital Marketing Specialist

Position Summary

We are seeking a detail-oriented and analytical Specialist, Performance Marketing to support paid search campaigns driving adoption of educational products and new student enrollment. This role will be responsible for the day-to-day execution, monitoring, optimization support, and reporting of paid search campaigns across multiple markets.

Reporting to the Principal, Performance Marketing , this position will work closely with internal stakeholders and agency partners to ensure campaigns are executed efficiently, performance goals are achieved, and optimization opportunities are identified. The ideal candidate has a strong foundation in paid search, a passion for data-driven marketing, and a desire to continue developing expertise across performance marketing disciplines.

Key Responsibilities

Campaign Execution & Management

Support the execution and ongoing management of paid search campaigns across Google Ads, Microsoft Ads, and SA360.

Implement campaign updates, ad copy changes, audience targeting adjustments, budget modifications, and other optimization recommendations.

Monitor campaign performance daily and identify performance trends, issues, or opportunities.

Conduct keyword research, search query analysis, and competitive monitoring.

Support campaign launches, promotions, enrollment season initiatives, and market-specific programs.

Ensure campaign settings, budgets, and targeting configurations are accurately maintained.

Optimization & Testing

Assist in the execution of testing initiatives across ad copy, bidding strategies, audiences, landing pages, and campaign structures.

Proactively analyze campaign data and provide recommendations to improve enrollment volume, conversion rates, and efficiency.

Support ongoing optimization efforts to improve Cost per Enrollment (CPE) and overall return on investment.

Stay informed on search platform updates, new features, AI-driven capabilities, and industry best practices.

Reporting & Analytics

Prepare recurring campaign reports and performance summaries.

Analyze campaign performance and communicate key insights to team members and stakeholders.

Monitor pacing and budget delivery to ensure media investments remain aligned with enrollment goals.

Validate campaign tracking and reporting accuracy.

Assist with forecasting, trend analysis, and performance investigations.

Agency & Cross-Functional Support

Collaborate with agency partners to ensure timely implementation of campaign updates and optimizations.

Participate in campaign reviews and performance discussions.

Partner with Analytics, Enrollment, Marketing, and Digital teams to support business objectives.

Coordinate campaign assets, creative approvals, and implementation requirements across stakeholders.

Operational Excellence

Perform quality assurance checks to ensure campaigns, tracking, and reporting are functioning correctly.

Maintain organized campaign documentation, testing logs, and performance records.

Support process improvement initiatives that increase efficiency and campaign effectiveness.

Assist in identifying automation opportunities that improve workflows and reporting.

Qualifications

Required

3-6 years of hands-on experience managing Paid Search (SEM) campaigns.

In-depth experience with Google Ads and Google Analytics.

Familiarity with bid management platforms such as SA360 is preferred.

Experience analyzing campaign performance data and making optimization recommendations.

Strong analytical and problem-solving skills.

Excellent attention to detail and organizational skills.

Proficiency with Excel and performance reporting tools.

Strong written and verbal communication skills.

Preferred

Experience with Microsoft Ads.

Exposure to Paid Social, Display, Programmatic, or other digital media channels.

Experience in lead generation, education, healthcare, financial services, or other performance-driven industries.

Familiarity with tagging, tracking, and attribution concepts.

Experience leveraging AI-powered tools to improve marketing workflows and campaign performance.

Key Competencies

Paid Search Fundamentals

Campaign Management

Performance Analysis

Data Interpretation

Quality Assurance

Problem Solving

Attention to Detail

Time Management

Communication

Collaboration

Continuous Learning

Digital Marketing

2835.FireCrawl Job Description: About Us Fieldguide is establishing a new state of trust for global commerce and capital markets through automating and streamlining the work of assurance and audit practitioners specifically within cybersecurity, privacy, and financial audit. Put simply, we build software for the people who enable trust between businesses. We’re based in San Francisco, CA, but built as a remote-first company that enables you to do your best work from anywhere. We're backed by top investors including Growth Equity at Goldman Sachs Alternatives, Bessemer Venture Partners, 8VC, Floodgate, Y Combinator, DNX Ventures, Global Founders Capital, Justin Kan, Elad Gil, and more. We value diversity — in backgrounds and in experiences. We need people from all backgrounds and walks of life to help build the future of audit and advisory. Fieldguide’s team is inclusive, driven, humble and supportive. We are deliberate and self-reflective about the kind of team and culture that we are building, seeking teammates that are not only strong in their own aptitudes but care deeply about supporting each other's growth. As an early stage start-up employee, you’ll have the opportunity to build out the future of business trust. We make audit practitioners’ lives easier by bringing together up to 50% of their work and giving them better work-life balance. If you share our values and enthusiasm for building a great culture and product, you will find a home at Fieldguide. About the Role We are looking for a performance marketer who is still in the accounts. You will own paid as a growth engine at Fieldguide: paid search, paid social, third-party media, landing page conversion, and the website as a demand tool. You will own the budget, the tests, the measurement, and the number. Our ambition is for paid to deliver 30 to 50% of high-quality MQLs and 30% of total pipeline. Today it delivers a fraction of that, which means the upside here is unusually clear. This is a hands-to-keyboard seat at a senior level. You will build and optimize, not brief an agency and report back. You will work alongside a peer who owns campaign demand (webinars, nurture, email), so you can go deep on performance rather than spreading thin. Two things we will be honest about. Our attribution is mid-rebuild, so part of this job is closing the measurement gap rather than inheriting a clean dashboard. And conversion optimization is coming back in-house, which means the testing program is yours to build rather than inherit. If either of those reads as a problem rather than an opportunity, this is not the seat. You are also someone who uses AI daily. Not as a novelty, but because you have built workflows that let one person do what a team used to. What You'll Do Own paid search. Google Ads and Microsoft Ads end to end: keyword and query strategy, bid management, ad copy, negatives hygiene, and landing page pairing. Drive CPA down and pipeline efficiency up, and be able to name the changes that did it. Own paid social. LinkedIn Ads end to end: audiences, creative testing, bidding, conversion tracking, and lead handoff. Build into emerging paid surfaces where the ICP actually is. Own third-party media and paid distribution. Programmatic display, native, OLV, DOOH, and content syndication, including the agency and trading desk relationships behind them. Own the conversion surface. Landing page performance, CRO test roadmap, the demo request path, form and gating strategy, and the website as a demand gen tool. Run the testing program in-house. Own the budget. Allocation across channels, in-quarter reallocation on a two-week read, monthly forecast versus actual, and agency spend management. Bring a kill-or-scale recommendation per channel and per vendor every quarter. Close the measurement gap. Build full-funnel paid measurement: attribution model, event-based tracking, and a clean line from spend to pipeline to revenue, in partnership with our RevOps and Marketing Ops teams. Use AI to multiply output. Ask whether AI can do the first 80% of every task. Build agentic monitoring that catches a spend or performance anomaly before a human notices. Share the workflows so the leverage compounds. Who You Are You have 5+ years in B2B performance or growth marketing, with clear ownership of a paid budget and a pipeline number. You have experience at the scale we are operating at: monthly paid spend and pipeline contribution in the range we are scaling into, not a few thousand dollars a month. You have hands-on, hands-to-keyboard paid experience. You have personally built, structured, and optimized paid search and paid social campaigns recently. You can walk someone into your account and explain the last three changes you made and why. You have full-funnel and revenue thinking. You can trace a paid dollar to MQL, SQL, SQO, and closed revenue, and you argue about efficiency rather than volume. You have real experience with attribution models and event-based tracking, ideally in an environment where the data was not clean. You have in-house CRO and landing page testing experience: cadence, backlog prioritization, and an honest win rate. You have HubSpot fluency, plus the ad platforms: Google Ads, Microsoft Ads, and LinkedIn Campaign Manager. You have vendor and agency management with teeth. You can hold an agency to a hypothesis and a metric, and end an engagement that isn't earning it. You have a specific, demonstrable AI practice in paid execution. You can show us the workflow, the inputs, and what it replaced. You hold yourself to a high bar. You are the first quality check on your own work, and you measure it against the best in the category, not against your last campaign. You have B2B experience with a considered, multi-stakeholder sale. Professional services, accounting, audit, or fintech is a plus. B2C or PLG-only is not a fit. What Great Looks Like Here We measure ourselves by outcomes, not effort. Opinions start the conversation; data ends it. Every program has a hypothesis, a metric, and an honest read, and we kill or scale on evidence. If that sounds like the way you already work, we should talk. More about Fieldguide: Fieldguide is a values-based company. Our values are: Fearless - Inspire & break down seemingly impossible walls. Fast - Launch fast with excellence, iterate to perfection. Lovable - ​​Deliver happiness & 11 star experiences. Owners - Execute & run the business with ownership. Win-win - Create mutual value & earn trust for life. Inclusive - Scale the best ideas with inclusive teams. Some of our benefits include: Competitive compensation packages with meaningful ownership Unlimited PTO 401k Wellness benefits starting your first day Technology & Work from Home reimbursement Flexible work schedules

2836.Job Title: Director of Product Growth & Digital Marketing
2836.FireCrawl Job Description: Salary Range: $150-175k + Equity Eligibility Benefits: FREE employee-only medical coverage, a 4% employer 401(k) match, and FREE short-term disability. Other incredible benefits HERE. Location: Remote in the continental US, with 25% nationwide travel Reports to: SVP, Strategy Who You Are We are looking for a highly analytical Growth Leader who bridges the gap between digital performance marketing and product-led growth. You feel completely at home digging into web and app analytics, running A/B tests, and working directly with software engineers to shape product features. If you have a proven track record of using behavioral marketing to build digital funnels that drive physical foot traffic and real-world revenue, we’re looking for you. Your Mission Transform Playbook ’s digital platform into a high-converting revenue engine that drives real-world, in-person utilization across two distinct audiences. You will own the digital-to-physical conversion path, architecting pre-login acquisition funnels to capture external demand, while simultaneously partnering with our Product team to build in-app mechanics that engage and monetize our audiences. You will also architect the centralized creative workflows, automation, and AI pipelines that allow these marketing engines to be spun up instantly at new properties with minimal operational lift. The Two Audiences You Will Own: The Public: External consumers and corporate groups. You need to capture their intent before they ever log in or download an app. You will use SEO, paid ads, and high-converting web infrastructure to drive discovery and direct bookings for our physical spaces (boardrooms, event halls, outdoor spaces) and public programming (ticketed events). Tenants: The employee population working for the companies inside our buildings. You will determine the mix of physical, experiential, and digital channels needed to capture their attention and drive initial registration. Because every building is different, you must ensure these acquisition strategies are highly targeted to fit the unique demographics, psychographics, and corporate cultures of the companies inside it. Once registered, you will define the in-app product mechanics, UI/UX booking flows, and automated lifecycle campaigns necessary to influence their daily behavior and turn this ecosystem into active users of our amenities, fitness centers, bookable spaces, and daily services. Outcomes You’ll Deliver: Build the Analytics Infrastructure: You will define the event schema, set up the tracking architecture, and establish exactly what metrics need to be measured to understand and influence user behavior. Optimize Digital Funnels: Map exactly where we are losing users across all service lines and build an immediate testing roadmap to fix conversion drop-offs. Capture the Captive Audience: Figure out how to get building tenants registered. You will design offline-to-online acquisition loops tailored to the specific demographic and psychographic makeup of a building's companies. Drive In-App Monetization: Design automated, behavioral lifecycle campaigns (email, push, retargeting) that get users to sign up for memberships and book spaces, services, and events, leveraging predictive analytics to identify and retain users. Guide the Product Roadmap: Work closely with engineers to build features that drive utilization. This includes developing logged-out discovery paths, smart recommendations, frictionless checkout flows, and seamless upsells. Architect Public Acquisition: Launch targeted paid campaigns and build un-gated landing pages. Capture external web traffic and convert it into qualified leads, physical space tours, and direct bookings. Command Visual Excellence & Content Workflows: Ensure our websites and digital platforms maintain a premium aesthetic everywhere. You will build scalable systems to capture and generate high-quality content. Scale AI & Automation Pipelines: Build a centralized stack integrating LLMs and our native CRM features to dynamically generate localized copy, retargeting sequences, and creative assets, ensuring properties operate at peak marketing quality without burdening the local teams. Establish Multi-Touch Attribution: Connect digital campaign performance and on-platform user behavior directly to physical space utilization and top-line property revenue. What You’ll Need: 6+ Years in Consumer Marketplace, Hospitality Tech, or O2O Growth: You have successfully scaled digital platforms that drive physical foot traffic, real-world space bookings, ticketing, or local service utilization. Note: This role is focused entirely on using digital funnels to drive in-person, real-world actions. Traditional B2B SaaS, physical e-commerce, or pure event marketing backgrounds are not a fit. Deep Product & Analytics Fluency: Advanced mastery of web and app analytics tools. You have hands-on experience setting up event tracking, defining requirements for engineers, and running systematic A/B tests. Pre-Login & Acquisition Experience: Direct experience building top-of-funnel discovery channels like SEO, paid media, and landing pages. You know how to capture user intent and drive action without forcing an initial app download. Key Competencies: Omnichannel Acquisition Skills: You know how to use physical and experiential touchpoints as measurable acquisition channels to drive digital registration. AI & Stack Automation: You know how to build AI tools and automation directly into a marketing stack to scale campaigns without needing a massive team. Creative Workflow Management: You know what a premium digital experience looks like, and you know how to scale it. You can manage visual standards across a nationwide portfolio and build seamless workflows to generate content at scale. Strategic Solo Operator: You thrive as a one-person shop. You will not have a department of direct reports; instead, you will rely on a network of cross-functional collaborators, freelancers, and AI tools to execute. You have the ability to operate as a nimble team of one, capable of configuring tracking, wireframing a UI flow, interpreting raw event data, and presenting clear insights to executive leadership. The In-Person Conversion Strategist: You deeply understand the psychological friction of getting a consumer to show up in person. You know how to use behavioral nudges, digital urgency, localized targeting, and frictionless UX to influence real-world actions. Data-Obsessed Optimizer: You instinctively look at behavioral analytics before making decisions. You rely on quantitative data and psychographic insights rather than assumptions to guide product roadmap requests and marketing investments. AI-First System Scaler: You refuse to rely on manual, one-off campaigns. You view AI, automation, and structured creative workflows as the foundational architecture required to rapidly deploy repeatable marketing across a nationwide portfolio. Compensation Additional Information Our Core Values: Playbook's culture is based on a shared respect for our lived values HERE. Fit with our values is a critical component of our hiring process, and you and all of our colleagues are expected to live our core values in interactions with team members, customers, and stakeholders. An assessment of how you have exhibited our values is also an important part of your performance review process. Our Commitment To You: Playbook is committed to building a team that represents a variety of backgrounds, perspectives, and skills. We know the more inclusive we are, the greater our impact will be! A Quick Note About Salaries: We list salaries based on a few key factors. These include location-specific budgets, market trends, team size, and the scope of the building. Since we’re a national company working with office properties of all shapes and sizes, the listed salary is tailored specifically to this role and may differ from similar-titled roles on our Careers Page. Curious or want to chat more about it? We promise to be open and transparent about these details throughout our interview process.

2837.FireCrawl Job Description: Where you’ll work: Remote (US) Marketing at GoTo At GoTo, our Marketing team shapes the company’s presence, voice, and vision—both inside GoTo and around the world. We use innovative, AI-driven insights and tools to connect with customers in meaningful ways and help grow our business. Here, creative problem-solving and fresh ideas are always encouraged and appreciated as we find new ways to share our story. Join our team, where your creativity and curiosity help us reach and inspire customers everywhere. About the role Every paid dollar we spend should move Grasshopper closer to its revenue goals, and you'll be the person who makes sure it does. As our Senior Performance Marketing Manager, you’ll own the strategy across paid search, paid social, and programmatic, and you’ll dig into the data to find what’s really driving growth. Funnel visibility, experiments, attribution, incrementality; you’ll roll up your sleeves to drive this forward, working alongside our agencies and teams across the business. If you love turning numbers into smart moves and consider yourself a self-starter, you’ll fit right in! Your Day to Day As our Senior Performance Marketing Manager you would be working on Paid go-to-market strategy Owning the end-to-end paid go-to-market strategy across paid search, paid social, and programmatic, and keeping it aligned with broader marketing and business objectives. Managing and allocating the paid media budget across channels, and optimizing for efficiency and performance against revenue and pipeline targets. Directing agency partners and internal stakeholders across, setting clear priorities, testing roadmaps, and performance standards so each channel is accountable to clear goals. Evaluating new channels, platforms, and tactics, including how AI-powered discovery is changing paid media, and deciding where to invest next. Developing testing roadmap from creative, audiences, channels, platforms, etc. based on data-driven insights and industry wide best practices. Analytics, measurement, and insights End-to-end funnel visibility: building and maintaining a clear, trusted view of the full funnel from impression to click to conversion, and identifying where performance breaks down. Performance reporting: owning channel reporting and dashboards, working alongside agencies and data partners to ensure the numbers are accurate, consistent, and decision-ready. Experiment design and analysis: designing structured tests across channels, creative, audiences, and bidding strategies, defining success metrics up front, and analyzing results with statistical rigor. Attribution and incrementality: evaluating how each channel contributes to revenue, running incrementality and lift testing, and challenging platform-reported results with independent analysis. Insights and recommendations: translating complex data into clear business narratives, with specific recommendations on budget, channel mix, and next steps for marketing leadership and cross-functional partners. What We're Looking For As our Senior Performance Marketing Manager your background will look like 7+ years of experience in paid media or performance marketing, with hands-on expertise in at least two of the following: paid search, paid social, or programmatic. A strong analytical foundation: you're deeply rooted in data and comfortable going from raw data to insight on your own, using tools such as GA4, SQL, BI and dashboarding tools, and Excel. Demonstrated experience designing and analyzing experiments, and applying attribution and incrementality methods (such as holdout tests, geo-lift, or marketing mix modeling) to inform budget decisions. A proven track record of owning and allocating multi-channel budgets against revenue or pipeline targets. Experience working with agency partners and holding them accountable to clear performance standards. Excellent communication and executive presence, with the ability to turn complex data into a clear story and present performance, trade-offs, and recommendations to senior leadership. Experience in B2B SaaS or subscription businesses is preferred. What We Offer At GoTo, we care about helping our people succeed at work and feel supported in life. Our employee benefits and programs are designed to support your well-being, growth, and sense of belonging. Here's what you can expect as part of our team: Comprehensive health benefits Generous paid time off, including paid holidays, volunteer days, quarterly self-care days, and company-designated no-meeting days Tuition reimbursement and access to instructor-led and on-demand learning and development programs The Thrive Global Wellness Program, a confidential Employee Assistance Program (EAP), a wellness app and one-on-one wellness coaching Employee-led communities and programs, including Employee Resource Groups (ERGs), GoTo Gives, and charitable matching We work hard to create an environment where everyone feels welcome, respected, and able to contribute. Building a culture of belonging isn't just something we talk about - it's part of how we work every day. Specific benefits and offerings may vary by country in line with local regulations and market practices.
